> Looking at `BRepGraph_CacheMesh`, it has a public default constructor, deleted copy operations, and inherits from `BRepGraph_Cache` which is a Transient-derived class based on its RTTI macro definition.
> 
> The real problem is that marking it as non-allocatable suppresses the destructor binding and prevents `CppDeletable` generation, but the auto-generated `to_handle` method for Transient classes still tries to use `OwnedPtr<Self>` — which doesn't work for a non-allocatable class. So when a class is both non-allocatable and Transient with a `to_handle` method, that method should be suppressed since you can't actually own the object. The same issue applies to `triangle_iterator` returning `OwnedPtr<Poly_CoherentTriPtr_Iterator>`, where the nested iterator class is non-allocatable. iterator is also non-allocatable (via the wildcard `Poly_CoherentTriPtr_*`? no — the main.rs matches `starts_with("Poly_CoherentTriPtr_")`). Wait the nested class is `Poly_CoherentTriPtr::Iterator` → mangled to `Poly_CoherentTriPtr_Iterator`. And main.rs matches `b.cpp_name.starts_with(&format!("{}_", nac))` where nac = "Poly_CoherentTriPtr", so "Poly_CoherentTriPtr_Iterator".starts_with("Poly_CoherentTriPtr_") = true. So the iterator is marked non-allocatable → constructors/destructors cleared → no CppDeletable. But `triangle_iterator` returns `OwnedPtr<...Iterator>`.
> 
> So there are two categories of the same underlying problem: a method returns/takes `OwnedPtr<T>` where T is non-allocatable (no CppDeletable). The real issue is that `triangle_iterator` returns an iterator by value in C++, but since the iterator has hidden operator new/delete, wrapping it in an OwnedPtr doesn't make sense — either suppress the method or handle it differently. The non-allocatable mechanism is meant to prevent constructing or owning these types, so returning an OwnedPtr of one is fundamentally broken and should be suppressed.

=== regenerate script ===
#!/bin/bash
# Regenerate OpenCASCADE bindings
#
# This script regenerates the FFI bindings for opencascade-sys.
# Run from the repository root.
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/regenerate-bindings.sh
#
# Requirements:
#   - Xcode command line tools (for libclang)
#   - OCCT headers built in target/OCCT/include

set -euo pipefail

# Repository root (script assumes it's run from repo root)
REPO_ROOT="${REPO_ROOT:-$(pwd)}"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

# Paths
OCCT_INCLUDE="$REPO_ROOT/target/OCCT/include"
OUTPUT_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/crates/opencascade-sys/generated"
CONFIG_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/crates/opencascade-sys/bindings.toml"

# Check prerequisites
if [[ ! -d "$OCCT_INCLUDE" ]]; then
    echo "Error: OCCT include directory not found at $OCCT_INCLUDE"
    echo "Run 'cargo build -p occt-sys' first to build OCCT"
    exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "Error: Config file not found at $CONFIG_FILE"
    exit 1
fi

# Build the generator in release mode to avoid a UB crash in the \`clang\` crate
# (v2.0.0) that only manifests in debug builds on Rust >= 1.78. See
# crates/opencascade-binding-generator/Cargo.toml for details.
echo "Building binding generator..."
cargo build --release -p opencascade-binding-generator

echo "Generating bindings from $CONFIG_FILE..."

# Clean generated directory
echo "Cleaning $OUTPUT_DIR..."
rm -f "$OUTPUT_DIR"/*.rs "$OUTPUT_DIR"/*.hxx "$OUTPUT_DIR"/*.cpp
# Also remove hidden generated files with empty basenames (e.g. \`.rs\`), which
# the \`*.rs\` glob doesn't match on most shells.
find "$OUTPUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '.rs' -delete 2>/dev/null || true
find "$OUTPUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '.hxx' -delete 2>/dev/null || true
find "$OUTPUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '.cpp' -delete 2>/dev/null || true

# Set library path for libclang on macOS
if [[ "$(uname)" == "Darwin" ]]; then
    XCODE_TOOLCHAIN="$(xcode-select -p)/Toolchains/XcodeDefault.xctoolchain/usr/lib"
    export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH="$XCODE_TOOLCHAIN:${DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
fi

# Run the generator
# Include both installed headers and build headers (needed for .pxx private headers)
OCCT_BUILD_INCLUDE="$REPO_ROOT/target/OCCT/build/include"
if [[ -d "$OCCT_BUILD_INCLUDE" ]]; then
    BUILD_INCLUDE_ARG=(-I "$OCCT_BUILD_INCLUDE")
else
    BUILD_INCLUDE_ARG=()
fi

"$REPO_ROOT/target/release/occt-bindgen" \
    --config "$CONFIG_FILE" \
    -I "$OCCT_INCLUDE" \
    "${BUILD_INCLUDE_ARG[@]}" \
    -o "$OUTPUT_DIR" \
    "$@"

echo ""
echo "Bindings generated in $OUTPUT_DIR"

    // 5. Remove excluded headers
    if !config.exclude_headers.is_empty() {
        let exclude_set: std::collections::HashSet<&str> =
            config.exclude_headers.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
        headers.retain(|path| {
            let filename = path.file_name().and_then(|f| f.to_str()).unwrap_or("");
            !exclude_set.contains(filename)
        });
    }

    // 6. Remove OCCT 8.0 deprecated backward-compatibility alias headers by content.
    //    These carry a standard banner comment; excluding them here avoids listing
    //    each of the ~970 alias headers individually in `exclude_headers`.
    if config.exclude_deprecated_headers {
        let before = headers.len();
        headers.retain(|path| !is_deprecated_alias_header(path));
        let excluded = before - headers.len();
        if excluded > 0 {
            println!("  Excluded {} deprecated alias headers (OCCT 8.0.0)", excluded);
        }
    }

    Ok(headers)
}

/// Detect an OCCT 8.0.0 deprecated backward-compatibility alias header (e.g.
/// `TColgp_HArray1OfPnt.hxx`, `TopTools_HSequenceOfShape.hxx`). These consist solely
/// of a `Standard_DEPRECATED` typedef forwarding to the canonical NCollection type and
/// carry the banner comment below. Matching the banner (rather than the raw
/// `Standard_HEADER_DEPRECATED` macro) avoids false positives such as `Standard_Macro.hxx`,
/// which merely defines that macro.
fn is_deprecated_alias_header(path: &Path) -> bool {
    match std::fs::read_to_string(path) {
        Ok(content) => content.contains("Deprecated typedef for backward compatibility"),
        Err(_) => false,
    }
}

## OCCT 8.0.0 deprecated backward-compatibility aliases

OCCT 8.0.0 moved ~970 backward-compat typedef headers into
`OCCT/src/Deprecated/NCollectionAliases/` (e.g. `TColgp_HArray1OfPnt.hxx` is now
just `typedef NCollection_HArray1<gp_Pnt> TColgp_HArray1OfPnt;`). OCCT's own 8.0 API
has already pivoted to the canonical `NCollection_...<T>` template names — method
signatures use `NCollection_List<TopoDS_Shape>` in ~190 headers vs. `TopTools_ListOfShape`
in only ~9 — and the deprecation messages explicitly say "use `NCollection_List<TopoDS_Shape>`
directly."

The binding generator excludes these alias headers automatically via
`exclude_deprecated_headers` (config flag, default true), which matches the standard
banner comment `"Deprecated typedef for backward compatibility"` in header content
(see `config::is_deprecated_alias_header`). This replaces the old approach of listing
each alias header individually in `exclude_headers`. `Standard_Macro.hxx` (defines the
macro) and `NCollection_Vector.hxx` (a template alias, not a concrete instantiation) are
intentionally *not* matched.

### KNOWN GAP — collections must be pivoted to canonical names (next task)

`codegen/collections.rs` currently keys its curated `known_collections()` map on the
**deprecated alias names** (`TopTools_ListOfShape`, `TColgp_Array1OfPnt`, ...) and emits
full method sets (`new`, `set_value`, `change_array1`, iterators, ...) under those names.
With `exclude_deprecated_headers` on, the parser no longer maps the canonical C++ type to
the alias, so method **signatures** resolve to the canonical mangled name
(`NCollection_Array1_gp_Pnt`, an opaque destructor-only type auto-emitted from usage) while
the collection **methods** remain orphaned under `TColgp_Array1OfPnt`. Net: `opencascade-sys`
still compiles/links, but collection method APIs are unreachable from canonically-typed
values. This is the confirmed direction but not yet implemented.

Plan to finish:
1. Rework `CollectionInfo`/`known_collections()` so each entry produces the canonical
   C++ template spelling (`NCollection_Array1<gp_Pnt>`), the canonical mangled Rust name
   via `config::template_alias_name` (`NCollection_Array1_gp_Pnt`), and module `NCollection`
   (→ `n_collection.rs`). FFI fn names use the mangled name; C++ wrappers use the template
   spelling (include `NCollection_Array1.hxx` etc., no deprecated header).
2. Keep the canonical names in `collection_type_names` so `generate_opaque_declarations`
   continues to skip them (dedup — the collection generator "owns" the type).
3. Maps need the hasher template arg, and it is present *conditionally*: e.g.
   `NCollection_DataMap<TopoDS_Shape, TopoDS_Shape, TopTools_ShapeMapHasher>` for shape keys,
   but `NCollection_DataMap<TCollection_AsciiString, int>` (no explicit hasher) for others.
   Match the exact spellings already emitted as opaque types in `ffi_types.rs`.
4. Add `HArray1`/`HSequence` `CollectionKind`s: `NCollection_HArray1<T>` publicly inherits
   `NCollection_Array1<T>` + `Standard_Transient`, so generate constructors
   (`new_int2(low, up)`, `new_int2_value`), `Array1()`/`change_array1() -> &mut Array1`
   accessors, and `to_handle` (handle types already registered via `template_instantiations`
   in `bindings.toml`). `NCollection_HSequence<T>` similarly wraps `NCollection_Sequence<T>`.
5. Port the high-level `opencascade` crate to the canonical names, e.g.:
   - `t_colgp::HArray1OfPnt` → `n_collection::HArray1_gp_Pnt` (with `NCollection_HArray1<gp_Pnt>`
     registered), `edge.rs::spline_from_points`.
   - `top_tools::HSequenceOfShape` → `n_collection::HSequence_TopoDS_Shape`, `wire.rs`.
   - `GeomAPI_Interpolate` ctor is now `new_handlencollectionharray1gppnt_bool_real(...)`.
   - Plus renames unrelated to collections: `stl_api::Writer::write` and
     `shape_analysis::FreeBounds::connect_edges_to_wires` no longer exist under those names —
     find the current generated equivalents.
````

The binding generator's collection method generation (`codegen/collections.rs`,
`known_collections()`) is keyed on OCCT alias names like `TopTools_ListOfShape`,
`TColgp_Array1OfPnt`. OCCT 8.0.0 deprecated all ~970 of these into

`NCollection_List<TopoDS_Shape>` / `NCollection_Array1<gp_Pnt>` (~190 headers use canonical
vs ~9 using the alias).

`exclude_deprecated_headers` (bindings.toml config flag, default true) now excludes deprecated
alias headers by matching the banner `"Deprecated typedef for backward compatibility"` in
header content. Consequence: collection method APIs get orphaned under alias names while
signatures reference canonical opaque types — collections must be re-keyed to canonical names.

**Why:** Confirmed with Seth (2026-07-21) that pivoting to canonical-only names is correct —
it matches OCCT's documented forward API. **How to apply:** the full plan (rework CollectionInfo
to canonical naming + template spelling, handle map hashers conditionally, add HArray1/HSequence
kinds, port the high-level `opencascade` crate) is written up in
`crates/opencascade-sys/PORTING.md` under "OCCT 8.0.0 deprecated backward-compatibility aliases".

On branch `rust-2024` (OCCT upgraded to V8_0_0_p1), `opencascade-sys` now builds, checks,
and links; all binding-generator tests pass. Fixes made:

- Non-allocatable classes: also set `has_to_handle = false` (main.rs) so `to_handle` (which
  takes `OwnedPtr<Self>`, needs CppDeletable) isn't emitted for them.

  allocatable nested classes (e.g. `Poly_CoherentTriPtr::Iterator`).
- Removed the parent-check in `rust.rs::generate_opaque_declarations` that suppressed
  CppDeletable for all nested types of non-allocatable parents (broke `BRepGraph_Tool::VertexUsage`,
  a public deletable typedef). Genuinely non-deletable nested types (e.g. the private uint64_t
  `BRepGraphInc_BitFlags::BlockType`) are listed explicitly in `non_allocatable_classes`.
- `gen` added to RUST_KEYWORDS (reserved in Rust 2024).
- TKDraw link error: the deprecated `Draw_MapOfAsciiString` alias routed a collection destructor
  to the unbuilt TKDraw toolkit — now excluded (superseded by `exclude_deprecated_headers`).

Remaining: the high-level `opencascade` crate still needs porting to OCCT 8.0 canonical
collection names — see [[collections-deprecated-aliases]] and PORTING.md.

56	    classes: &[&ParsedClass],
57	    functions: &[&crate::model::ParsedFunction],
58	    handle_able_classes: &HashSet<String>,
59	) -> CollectedTypes {
60	    let mut result = CollectedTypes {
61	        classes: BTreeSet::new(),
62	        handles: BTreeSet::new(),
63	    };
64	
65	    for class in classes {
66	        // Add Handle type for classes that are transient (can be wrapped in Handle)
67	        // Handle types with protected destructors are included because Handle<T>
68	        // manages lifetime via reference counting, not direct delete.
69	        if handle_able_classes.contains(&class.name) {
70	            result.handles.insert(class.name.clone());
71	        }
72	
73	        crate::model::for_each_type_in_class(class, &mut |ty| {
74	            collect_types_from_type(ty, &mut result);
75	        });
76	    }
77	
78	    for func in functions {
79	        crate::model::for_each_type_in_function(func, &mut |ty| {
80	            collect_types_from_type(ty, &mut result);
81	        });
82	    }
83	
84	    result
85	}

87	/// Recursively collect OCCT class and Handle types from a type.
88	/// Uses \`visit_inner\` to unwrap reference/pointer wrappers.
89	fn collect_types_from_type(ty: &Type, collected: &mut CollectedTypes) {
90	    // Skip unbindable types (arrays, rvalue refs, etc.) — but NOT streams,
91	    // which are manually-defined opaque types that we DO want to collect.
92	    if ty.is_unbindable() {
93	        return;
94	    }
95	
96	    ty.visit_inner(&mut |inner| {
97	        match inner {
98	            Type::Class(name) => {
99	                // Skip primitive types, void pointer types, and template instantiations (e.g., NCollection_Shared<...>)
100	                if !is_primitive_type(name) && !name.contains('<') && !crate::model::is_void_type_name(name) {
101	                    collected.classes.insert(name.clone());
102	                }
103	            }
104	            Type::Handle(name) => {
105	                // Record the Handle type AND the inner class
106	                if !name.contains('<') {
107	                    collected.handles.insert(name.clone());
108	                    collected.classes.insert(name.clone());
109	                }
110	            }
111	            _ => {}
112	        }
113	    });
114	}

116	/// Check if a type name is a primitive (not an OCCT class)
117	pub fn is_primitive_type(name: &str) -> bool {
118	    matches!(
119	        name,
120	        // Rust primitive names
121	        "bool" | "i8" | "u8" | "i32" | "u32" | "u16" | "i64" | "u64" | "f32" | "f64" | "char" | "c_char" |
122	        "c_long" | "c_ulong" |
123	        // C++ primitive names (may appear from canonical type resolution)
124	        "double" | "float" | "int" | "unsigned int" | "long" | "unsigned long" |
125	        "long long" | "unsigned long long" | "short" | "unsigned short" |
126	        "signed char" | "unsigned char"
127	    )
128	}

139	/// ffi_extern_TK*.rs for extern "C" function declarations.

150	    all_functions: &[&crate::model::ParsedFunction],

152	    collections: &[super::collections::CollectionInfo],

156	    handle_able_classes: &HashSet<String>,
157	    extra_typedef_names: &HashSet<String>,
158	    non_allocatable_classes: &HashSet<String>,
159	    module_to_toolkit: &std::collections::HashMap<String, String>,
160	) -> (String, Vec<NestedTypeInfo>, Vec<(String, String)>) {
161	    // Get all classes with protected destructors, and merge in non-allocatable classes

165	    }
166	    let all_enum_names = &symbol_table.all_enum_names;
167	    let collection_type_names: HashSet<String> = collections.iter()

/// Parse a typedef name to extract collection info if it's a known collection type
pub fn parse_collection_typedef(typedef_name: &str) -> Option<CollectionInfo> {
    let known = known_collections();
    let metadata = known.get(typedef_name)?;
    
    // Extract module from typedef name (e.g., "TopTools" from "TopTools_ListOfShape")
    let (module_cpp, module) = if let Some(underscore_pos) = typedef_name.find('_') {
        let module_cpp = &typedef_name[..underscore_pos];
        (module_cpp, crate::module_graph::module_to_rust_name(module_cpp))
    } else {
        return None;
    };
    
    // Extract short name (e.g., "ListOfShape" from "TopTools_ListOfShape")
    let short_name = crate::type_mapping::short_name_for_module(typedef_name, module_cpp);
    
    match metadata {
        CollectionMetadata::Simple { element_type, kind } => {
            Some(CollectionInfo {
                typedef_name: typedef_name.to_string(),
                module,
                short_name,
                element_type: element_type.to_string(),
                element_module: type_to_module(element_type),
                value_type: None,
                value_module: None,
                kind: *kind,
            })
        }
        CollectionMetadata::DataMap { key_type, value_type, kind } => {
            Some(CollectionInfo {
                typedef_name: typedef_name.to_string(),
                module,
                short_name,
                element_type: key_type.to_string(),  // key_type stored in element_type
                element_module: type_to_module(key_type),
                value_type: Some(value_type.to_string()),
                value_module: Some(type_to_module(value_type)),
                kind: *kind,
            })
        }
    }
}

/// Get all known collection types
pub fn all_known_collections() -> Vec<CollectionInfo> {
    let mut result: Vec<_> = known_collections()
        .keys()
        .filter_map(|name| parse_collection_typedef(name))
        .collect();
    // Sort for deterministic ordering
    result.sort_by(|a, b| a.typedef_name.cmp(&b.typedef_name));
    result
}

/// Split a template spelling `Base<A, B, ...>` into its base name and the list of
/// top-level template arguments (respecting nested `<>`). Returns `None` if the
/// spelling is not a `Base<...>` template.
fn split_template_args(spelling: &str) -> Option<(String, Vec<String>)> {
    let open = spelling.find('<')?;
    if !spelling.ends_with('>') {
        return None;
    }
    let base = spelling[..open].trim().to_string();
    let inner = &spelling[open + 1..spelling.len() - 1];
    let mut args = Vec::new();
    let mut depth = 0i32;
    let mut start = 0usize;
    for (i, c) in inner.char_indices() {
        match c {
            '<' => depth += 1,
            '>' => depth -= 1,
            ',' if depth == 0 => {
                args.push(inner[start..i].trim().to_string());
                start = i + 1;
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    let last = inner[start..].trim();
    if !last.is_empty() {
        args.push(last.to_string());
    }
    Some((base, args))
}

/// Parse a canonical `NCollection_*<...>` template spelling into a `CollectionInfo`.
/// The mangled `typedef_name` is derived via `config::template_alias_name`, matching
/// the opaque type name that method signatures resolve to. Returns `None` for
/// spellings that are not recognized NCollection collection templates.
pub fn parse_canonical_collection(spelling: &str) -> Option<CollectionInfo> {
    let (base, args) = split_template_args(spelling)?;
    let kind = CollectionKind::from_template_base(&base)?;
    if args.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }

    let typedef_name = crate::config::template_alias_name(spelling);
    // Short name drops the "NCollection_" prefix, e.g. "List_TopoDS_Shape".
    let short_name = typedef_name
        .strip_prefix("NCollection_")
        .unwrap_or(&typedef_name)
        .to_string();

    let (element_type, value_type) = if kind.is_data_map() {
        // DataMap<Key, Value[, Hasher]> / IndexedDataMap<Key, Value[, Hasher]>
        let value = args.get(1)?.clone();
        (args[0].clone(), Some(value))
    } else {
        // List/Sequence/Array1/Array2/HArray1/HSequence<Elem>, Map/IndexedMap<Key[, Hasher]>
        (args[0].clone(), None)
    };

    Some(CollectionInfo {
        typedef_name,
        cpp_spelling: spelling.to_string(),
        module: "n_collection".to_string(),
        short_name,
        element_module: type_to_module(&element_type),
        value_module: value_type.as_deref().map(type_to_module),
        element_type,
        value_type,
        kind,
    })
}

/// A curated seed of canonical collection spellings to always materialize, even if
/// they are not (yet) auto-discovered from method signatures. Kept small — most
/// collections are discovered automatically via [`discover_collections`].
fn seed_collection_spellings() -> &'static [&'static str] {
    &[
        "NCollection_Array1<gp_Pnt>",
        "NCollection_Array1<double>",
        "NCollection_HArray1<gp_Pnt>",
        "NCollection_HArray1<double>",
        "NCollection_List<TopoDS_Shape>",
        "NCollection_Sequence<TopoDS_Shape>",
        "NCollection_HSequence<TopoDS_Shape>",
    ]
}

/// Discover collections to generate from the set of referenced NCollection template
/// spellings, keeping only those whose element/key/value types are bindable
/// (per `is_known_type`). The curated seed spellings are always included.
pub fn discover_collections(
    referenced_spellings: &std::collections::HashSet<String>,
    is_known_type: impl Fn(&str) -> bool,
) -> Vec<CollectionInfo> {
    let mut by_name: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, CollectionInfo> =
        std::collections::BTreeMap::new();

    let candidates = referenced_spellings
        .iter()
        .map(|s| s.as_str())
        .chain(seed_collection_spellings().iter().copied());

    for spelling in candidates {
        let Some(info) = parse_canonical_collection(spelling) else {
            continue;
        };
        // Gate on bindability: the C++ wrapper and FFI can only be generated when the
        // element (and value, for maps) types are known bound types or primitives.
        let elem_ok = is_primitive_element(&info.element_type) || is_known_type(&info.element_type);
        let value_ok = info
            .value_type
            .as_ref()
            .map(|v| is_primitive_element(v) || is_known_type(v))
            .unwrap_or(true);
        if !elem_ok || !value_ok {
            continue;
        }
        by_name.entry(info.typedef_name.clone()).or_insert(info);
    }

    by_name.into_values().collect()
}

pub fn rust_element_type(cpp_type: &str) -> &str {

    match cpp_type {
        "Standard_Real" => "f64",
        "Standard_Integer" => "i32",
        "Standard_Boolean" => "bool",

    }

/// Returns true if the element type is a C++ primitive that maps to a Rust native type.
pub fn is_primitive_element(cpp_type: &str) -> bool {

    matches!(cpp_type, "Standard_Real" | "Standard_Integer" | "Standard_Boolean")
}

pub fn rust_element_type(cpp_type: &str) -> &str {

    match cpp_type {
        "Standard_Real" | "double" => "f64",
        "Standard_Integer" | "int" => "i32",
        "Standard_Boolean" | "bool" => "bool",
        "Standard_ShortReal" | "float" => "f32",
        _ => cpp_type,
    }
}

/// Returns true if the element type is a C++ primitive that maps to a Rust native type.
pub fn is_primitive_element(cpp_type: &str) -> bool {

    matches!(
        cpp_type,
        "Standard_Real" | "double"
            | "Standard_Integer" | "int"
            | "Standard_Boolean" | "bool"
            | "Standard_ShortReal" | "float"
    )
}

/// A curated seed of canonical collection spellings to always materialize, even if
```

```
/// Scan all class and free-function signatures for referenced `NCollection_*<...>`
/// template spellings. These are the exact spellings OCCT's own 8.0 API uses (with
/// correct hasher arguments), so materializing collections from them keeps the FFI
/// type names aligned with what method signatures resolve to.
pub fn collect_collection_spellings(
    classes: &[&crate::model::ParsedClass],
    functions: &[&crate::model::ParsedFunction],
) -> std::collections::HashSet<String> {
    fn add(ty: &crate::model::Type, out: &mut std::collections::HashSet<String>) {
        ty.visit_inner(&mut |inner| {
            if let crate::model::Type::Class(name) = inner {
                if name.starts_with("NCollection_") && name.contains('<') {
                    out.insert(name.clone());
                }
            }
        });
    }
    let mut out = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    for c in classes {
        crate::model::for_each_type_in_class(c, &mut |ty| add(ty, &mut out));
    }
    for f in functions {
        crate::model::for_each_type_in_function(f, &mut |ty| add(ty, &mut out));
    }
    out
}

/// A curated seed of canonical collection spellings to always materialize, even if

> All 22 generator tests are passing and the signatures now correctly reference the same canonical type that the collection generates methods for—the split-brain issue is resolved. The foundational refactor for canonical collections is complete with auto-discovery, proper naming, full method sets, and successful builds. Next up is handling HArray1.
> 
> HSequence full support with handle and element methods is deferred since it's needed for the high-level crate port. The high-level `opencascade` crate migration to canonical names is substantial and depends on HArray1/HSequence for edge.rs and wire.rs, plus other collection references like top_tools::ListOfShape need updating too. Given the session length and the major working piece I've delivered, I should update the plan in PORTING.md to reflect what's done and report the status clearly before deciding whether to tackle HArray1/HSequence now or defer it.
> 
> The core challenge with HArray1 is coordinating the base type generation—if both the collection generator and template_instantiations produce it, there's a conflict. The solution is to let the collection own the base type and destructor, but then the handle type (HandleNCollectionHArray1gpPnt) needs to come from somewhere for to_handle and constructor parameters. When the parser encounters Handle(NCollection_HArray1<gp_Pnt>), it generates the handle type, so I need to figure out whether the collection generator should produce that or if template_instantiations should.
> 
> Since NCollection_HArray1<gp_Pnt> inherits Standard_Transient and needs to be registered as handle-able, template_instantiations is what tells the generator that's possible. The cleanest approach is to keep template_instantiations for handle type generation and handle-able registration, but have the collection generator produce only the element methods and to_handle, referencing the base type that template_instantiations already created.
> 
> The challenge is that generate_cpp_collection unconditionally emits _new and _destructor, so I'd need to conditionally skip those for handle kinds across the FFI and Rust re-export layers too. Given the scope of this session, I'm going to defer HArray1/HSequence and the high-level crate port, documenting what's been delivered and what remains in PORTING.md. But let me think through this once more.
> 
> The high-level crate is still broken because it references old names, and even if I ported the non-HArray1 parts like the collection renames and stl write logic, edge.rs and wire.rs would still fail without HArray1 and HSequence support. So the crate won't fully build anyway. Given the session length and how much work I've already done, the cleanest path is to finalize PORTING.md with the canonical collections foundation marked as complete and HArray1/HSequence plus the full port as documented remaining work.

## 🤖 Assistant
<!-- msg_011CdGMAfCj2yW8Z2gRze7cQ -->

Now I have the full concrete picture. Here's the explanation.

## How `HArray1`/`HSequence` worked *before* the upgrade

They were **never collections** in the generator's eyes — they were ordinary classes.

Pre-8.0, `TColgp_HArray1OfPnt.hxx` used OCCT's `DEFINE_HARRAY1` macro, which expands to a **concrete, named class**:

```cpp
class TColgp_HArray1OfPnt : public TColgp_Array1OfPnt, public Standard_Transient {
  ... DEFINE_STANDARD_RTTIEXT(TColgp_HArray1OfPnt, ...) ...
};
```

clang parsed that as a normal class, so the generator's **standard class-binding path** produced everything, keyed on the concrete name `TColgp_HArray1OfPnt` (from [the old generated code](crates/opencascade-sys/generated/t_colgp.rs)):
- constructors — `new()`, `new_int2(lower, upper)`, `new_int2_type(...)`, `new_array1ofpnt(...)`
- accessors — `array1() -> &Array1OfPnt`, `change_array1() -> &mut Array1OfPnt`
- `CppDeletable`, `dynamic_type()`, and a `to_handle()` + `HandleTColgpHArray1OfPnt` type (because it derived from `Standard_Transient` with a concrete name)

One mechanism produced the base type, the handle, and all methods **coherently**, because it was one concrete class.

## Why 8.0 broke it

The header is now just:
```cpp
typedef NCollection_HArray1<gp_Pnt> TColgp_HArray1OfPnt;
```
There's no named class anymore — the members live on the **class template** `NCollection_HArray1<T>`. The generator doesn't parse/instantiate templates as classes, so no constructors/accessors/handle get generated; you get an opaque destructor-only type. (And the deprecated typedef header is now excluded outright.)

## The actual porting issues

`NCollection_HArray1<gp_Pnt>` is **two things at once** — a collection (Array1 element methods) *and* a Transient handle type (`to_handle` + a `Handle`). Before, both came from one class binding. Now the responsibilities are split across two generator mechanisms that **both want to define the same base type**, which collides:

1. **Base-type ownership / duplication.** The `template_instantiations` entry I added to [bindings.toml](crates/opencascade-sys/bindings.toml) already emits, for `NCollection_HArray1<gp_Pnt>`:
   - `pub struct NCollection_HArray1_gp_Pnt` + its `_destructor`
   - the handle type `HandleNCollectionHArray1gpPnt` (+ clone/is_null/CppDeletable)

   If the **collection** mechanism also emits that base struct + `_new`/`_destructor`, you get a duplicate `pub struct` (Rust E0428) and a duplicate destructor (C++ ODR violation). That's why `discover_collections` currently `continue`s on `is_handle()` kinds — naive coexistence doesn't compile.

2. **Two manglers must line up.** The collection base type keeps underscores (`NCollection_HArray1_gp_Pnt`), but the handle mangler *drops* them (`gp_Pnt` → `HandleNCollectionHArray1gpPnt`). A collection-generated `to_handle` must return exactly the handle type the `GeomAPI_Interpolate` ctor parameter already references (`HandleNCollectionHArray1gpPnt`), so the two naming schemes have to be threaded together deliberately.

3. **The accessor shape changed.** The old API exposed `change_array1() -> &mut Array1OfPnt` (a distinct `TColgp_Array1OfPnt`). In the canonical world the natural move is for `HArray1_gp_Pnt` to *be* an `Array1_gp_Pnt` (it inherits it) and expose `set_value` directly, or to return `&mut Array1_gp_Pnt` — a small API-shape decision that also ripples into the high-level crate's `edge.rs`.

## The two ways to resolve it (in [PORTING.md](crates/opencascade-sys/PORTING.md))

- **(a) Collection owns everything** — drop the `template_instantiations` entries and have the collection generate the base type *and* the handle machinery (most like the pre-8.0 single-owner model, but the collection code has to learn to emit handle types).
- **(b) Split ownership** — keep `template_instantiations` for the base+handle type, and have the collection contribute *only* element methods + `to_handle`, suppressing its own struct/`_new`/`_destructor` for handle kinds. use crate::primitives::make_point;
use glam::DVec3;
use opencascade_sys::{geom, t_colgp};

pub struct Surface {
    pub(crate) inner: opencascade_sys::OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomSurface>,
}

impl Surface {
    pub fn bezier(poles: impl IntoIterator<Item = impl IntoIterator<Item = DVec3>>) -> Self {
        let poles: Vec<Vec<_>> =
            poles.into_iter().map(|poles| poles.into_iter().collect()).collect();

        let mut pole_array = t_colgp::Array2OfPnt::new_int4(
            0,
            poles.len() as i32 - 1,
            0,
            poles.first().map(|first| first.len()).unwrap_or(0) as i32 - 1,
        );

        for (row, poles) in poles.iter().enumerate() {
            for (column, pole) in poles.iter().enumerate() {
                let pole = &make_point(*pole);
                pole_array.set_value(row as i32, column as i32, pole);
            }
        }

        let bezier = geom::BezierSurface::new_array2ofpnt(&pole_array);
        let handle = geom::BezierSurface::to_handle(bezier);
        let inner = handle.to_handle_surface();

        Self { inner }
    }
}
```
</details>

use glam::DVec2;
use opencascade_sys::{law, t_colgp};

use crate::primitives::make_point2d;

/// Creates a Law_Function handle from a set of (parameter, radius) pairs.
/// Used for variable-radius pipe shell sweeps and variable fillets.
#[must_use]
pub(crate) fn law_function_from_graph(
    pairs: impl IntoIterator<Item = (f64, f64)>,
) -> opencascade_sys::OwnedPtr<law::HandleLawFunction> {
    let pairs: Vec<(f64, f64)> = pairs.into_iter().collect();
    let n = pairs.len() as i32;

    let mut array = t_colgp::Array1OfPnt2d::new_int2(1, n);
    for (i, &(param, radius)) in pairs.iter().enumerate() {
        let pnt2d = make_point2d(DVec2::new(param, radius));
        array.set_value(i as i32 + 1, &pnt2d);
    }

    let mut interpol = law::Interpol::new();
    interpol.set_array1ofpnt2d_bool(&array, false);

    let handle = law::Interpol::to_handle(interpol);
    handle.to_handle_function()
}
```
</details>

fn collect_template_class_types(parsed: &[model::ParsedHeader]) -> HashSet<String> {
    let mut templates = HashSet::new();

    for header in parsed {
        model::for_each_type_in_header(header, &mut |ty| {
            ty.visit_inner(&mut |inner| {
                if let model::Type::Class(name) = inner {
                    if name.contains('<') {
                        templates.insert(name.clone());
                    }
                }
            });
        });

/// Scan all class and free-function signatures for referenced `NCollection_*<...>`
/// template spellings. These are the exact spellings OCCT's own 8.0 API uses (with
/// correct hasher arguments), so materializing collections from them keeps the FFI
/// type names aligned with what method signatures resolve to.
pub fn collect_collection_spellings(
    classes: &[&crate::model::ParsedClass],
    functions: &[&crate::model::ParsedFunction],
) -> std::collections::HashSet<String> {
    fn add(ty: &crate::model::Type, out: &mut std::collections::HashSet<String>) {
        ty.visit_inner(&mut |inner| {
            if let crate::model::Type::Class(name) = inner {
                if name.starts_with("NCollection_") && name.contains('<') {
                    out.insert(name.clone());
                }
            }
        });
    }
    let mut out = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    for c in classes {
        crate::model::for_each_type_in_class(c, &mut |ty| add(ty, &mut out));
    }
    for f in functions {
        crate::model::for_each_type_in_function(f, &mut |ty| add(ty, &mut out));
    }
    out
}

/// Discover collections to generate from the set of referenced NCollection template
/// spellings, keeping only those whose element/key/value types are bindable
/// (per `is_known_type`). The curated seed spellings are always included.
pub fn discover_collections(
    referenced_spellings: &std::collections::HashSet<String>,
    is_known_type: impl Fn(&str) -> bool,
) -> Vec<CollectionInfo> {
    let mut by_name: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, CollectionInfo> =
        std::collections::BTreeMap::new();

    let candidates = referenced_spellings
        .iter()
        .map(|s| s.as_str())
        .chain(seed_collection_spellings().iter().copied());

    for spelling in candidates {
        let Some(info) = parse_canonical_collection(spelling) else {
            continue;
        };
        // Gate on bindability: the C++ wrapper and FFI can only be generated when the
        // element (and value, for maps) types are known bound types or primitives.
        let elem_ok = is_primitive_element(&info.element_type) || is_known_type(&info.element_type);
        let value_ok = info
            .value_type
            .as_ref()
            .map(|v| is_primitive_element(v) || is_known_type(v))
            .unwrap_or(true);
        if !elem_ok || !value_ok {
            continue;
        }
        by_name.entry(info.typedef_name.clone()).or_insert(info);
    }

    by_name.into_values().collect()
}
```

**After:**
```
/// Discover collections to generate from the set of referenced NCollection template
/// spellings, keeping only those whose element/key/value types are bindable. A type is
/// bindable if it is a primitive, or `header_of` returns the C++ header that defines it
/// (i.e. it is a known parsed class). The resolved header is stored so the C++ wrapper
/// includes the correct file (element headers are not always `{TypeName}.hxx`). The
/// curated seed spellings are always included.
pub fn discover_collections(
    referenced_spellings: &std::collections::HashSet<String>,
    header_of: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String>,
) -> Vec<CollectionInfo> {
    let mut by_name: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, CollectionInfo> =
        std::collections::BTreeMap::new();

    let candidates = referenced_spellings
        .iter()
        .map(|s| s.as_str())
        .chain(seed_collection_spellings().iter().copied());

    for spelling in candidates {
        let Some(mut info) = parse_canonical_collection(spelling) else {
            continue;
        };
        // Gate on bindability: the C++ wrapper and FFI can only be generated when the
        // element (and value, for maps) types are primitives or known classes with a
        // resolvable defining header.
        let element_header = if is_primitive_element(&info.element_type) {
            None
        } else {
            match header_of(&info.element_type) {
                Some(h) => Some(h),
                None => continue,
            }
        };
        let value_header = match &info.value_type {
            Some(v) if is_primitive_element(v) => None,
            Some(v) => match header_of(v) {
                Some(h) => Some(h),
                None => continue,
            },
            None => None,
        };
        info.element_header = element_header;
        info.value_header = value_header;
        by_name.entry(info.typedef_name.clone()).or_insert(info);
    }

    by_name.into_values().collect()
}
```

        ));

/// Filter out the FILE_NAME line (and its continuation lines) from a STEP file,
/// since it contains a timestamp that changes on every run.
fn normalize_step(content: &str) -> String {
    let mut result = String::new();
    let mut in_file_name = false;
    for line in content.lines() {
        if line.starts_with("FILE_NAME(") {
            in_file_name = true;
            continue;
        }
        if in_file_name {
            if line.contains(");") {
                in_file_name = false;
            }
            continue;
        }
        result.push_str(line);
        result.push('\n');
    }
    result
}

## Porting a client of older opencascade-rs to the OCCT 8.0 bindings

If you have downstream Rust code written against the pre-8.0 bindings, here are the
high-level, client-visible changes to expect (all mechanical; the compiler will point you
at each site):

### 1. Collections moved to canonical `n_collection::` names
OCCT 8.0 deprecated the `TColgp_*` / `TColStd_*` / `TopTools_*` collection aliases and
uses the canonical `NCollection_*<T>` templates directly. The bindings follow suit — every
collection now lives in the `n_collection` module named after the template + element:

| Old | New |
|-----|-----|
| `t_colgp::Array1OfPnt` | `n_collection::Array1_gp_Pnt` |
| `t_colgp::Array2OfPnt` | `n_collection::Array2_gp_Pnt` |
| `t_colgp::Array1OfPnt2d` | `n_collection::Array1_gp_Pnt2d` |
| `t_col_std::Array1OfReal` | `n_collection::Array1_double` |
| `top_tools::ListOfShape` | `n_collection::List_TopoDS_Shape` |
| `top_tools::SequenceOfShape` | `n_collection::Sequence_TopoDS_Shape` |
| `top_tools::IndexedMapOfShape` | `n_collection::IndexedMap_TopoDS_Shape` |

Shape-keyed maps carry the hasher in their name, e.g. a `TopExp::MapShapes` out-parameter is
`n_collection::IndexedMap_TopoDS_Shape_TopTools_ShapeMapHasher` (not the bare `IndexedMap_TopoDS_Shape`).
Collections of scalars are supported too (`List_int`, `Map_int`, `Sequence_double`,
`DataMap_TopoDS_Shape_int`, …); scalar map lookups return `Option<T>` by value.

### 2. Handle types use the `Handle_<C++name>` scheme
`HandleGeomCurve` → `Handle_Geom_Curve`, `HandleGeomSurface` → `Handle_Geom_Surface`,
`HandleLawFunction` → `Handle_Law_Function`, etc. (matches OCCT's own classic `Handle_X`
spelling). Handle *methods* (`get`, `get_mut`, `is_null`, `to_handle_*`, `downcast_to_*`)
are unchanged.

### 3. `HArray1`/`HSequence` are collections now
Formerly stand-alone classes (`t_colgp::HArray1OfPnt`), they are `n_collection::HArray1_gp_Pnt`
/ `HSequence_TopoDS_Shape`, etc. Because `NCollection_HArray1<T>` *is* an `NCollection_Array1<T>`,
call element methods directly: `array.change_array1().set_value(i, v)` becomes
`array.set_value(i, v)`. `to_handle(owned)` and (on the resulting handle) `get()`/`get_mut()`
work as before.

### 4. Overloaded method/ctor suffixes follow the new element names
Suffixes are derived from the canonical element type, so:
`BezierCurve::new_array1ofpnt` → `new_array1_gp_pnt`,
`BezierSurface::new_array2ofpnt` → `new_array2_gp_pnt`,
`MakeFillet::add_array1ofpnt2d_edge` → `add_array1_gp_pnt2d_edge`,
`Interpol::set_array1ofpnt2d_bool` → `set_array1_gp_pnt2d_bool`,
`GeomAPI_Interpolate::new_handletcolgpharray1ofpnt_bool_real` →
`new_handlencollectionharray1gppnt_bool_real`.

### 5. Deprecated OCCT symbols are gone — use the 8.0 replacement
Deprecated headers aren't bound at all (see the "OCCT 8.0.0 deprecated ..." section above).
Notable API relocations/signature changes encountered:
- `GCE2d_MakeSegment` (and other `GCE2d_*` builders) → the consolidated `GC_*` equivalents,
  e.g. `gce2d::MakeSegment` → `gc::MakeSegment2d` (value returns `Handle_Geom2d_TrimmedCurve`).
- `ShapeAnalysis_FreeBounds::connect_edges_to_wires` now **returns** the wire
  `Handle_NCollection_HSequence_TopoDS_Shape` and takes 3 args `(edges, tol, shared)`
  (the wires out-parameter was removed).
- `StlAPI_Writer::write` → `write_shape_charptr_progressrange(shape, path, progress)`.
- `GeomAPI_Interpolate::load_vec2_bool` → `load(initial_tangent, final_tangent, scale)`.
```
</details>

## Final status

**Full workspace builds; all tests pass** — 22 binding-generator tests, 33 workspace tests, 0 failures.

### What the port required (and surfaced)

**High-level crate** — mechanical renames across `edge.rs`, `wire.rs`, `shape.rs`, `surface.rs`, `face.rs`, `solid.rs`, `law_function.rs` plus the `bottle` example: collection names → `n_collection::*`, handles → `Handle_*`, and the OCCT 8.0 API changes (`FreeBounds::connect_edges_to_wires` now returns the wire sequence; `stl write` → `write_shape_charptr_progressrange`; `GCE2d_MakeSegment` → `gc::MakeSegment2d`; `Interpolate::load`).

**Three deeper generator fixes uncovered during the port:**
1. **Auto-discovery was a no-op** — it scanned binding types, but template names are mangled *before* codegen, so only the 7 seeded collections materialized. Fixed to use `template_instantiations.keys()` (the pre-rewrite spellings) → **228 collections** now generate with full methods.
2. **Element headers** — inferring `{Type}.hxx` was wrong (`Standard_DumpValue` lives in `Standard_Dump.hxx`). Now resolved from each class's actual `source_header`.
3. **Your "rare" pushback was right** — `List<int>` (50 refs), `DataMap<TopoDS_Shape,int>` (22), `Sequence<double>`, etc. are heavily used in the public API (`BOPDS::faces`, `BRepBuilderAPI::res_ind`, …). I removed the gate and added **full primitive-scalar collection support**: primitive-aware FFI/re-export types, and `find`/`find_key`/iterator `next` return `Option<T>`/`&T` by copy (borrowing the pointee) instead of `OwnedPtr<primitive>`. I also added `get`/`get_mut` + handle lifetime machinery for the collection handle types (which fell through the per-toolkit ownership check).

**Golden files** — regenerated all 23 for OCCT 8.0. Verified the only differences were the `7.9`→`8.0` version string in `PRODUCT` entities and ~1e-16 floating-point noise (absorbed by the comparison's numeric tolerance) — no geometry regressions.

[PORTING.md](crates/opencascade-sys/PORTING.md) now has the requested **"Porting a client of older opencascade-rs to OCCT 8.0"** section — a client-facing table of collection/handle renames, the `HArray1`/`HSequence`-are-collections change, method-suffix changes, and the deprecated→8.0 API relocations.

1	# Porting C++ OCCT Code to Rust with opencascade-sys
2	
3	This guide covers translating C++ code that uses OpenCASCADE Technology (OCCT)
4	into Rust using the \`opencascade-sys\` crate.
5	
6	## Module Structure
7	
8	OCCT C++ classes like \`BRepBuilderAPI_MakeEdge\` are re-exported in Rust modules
9	derived from the package prefix. The module name is the snake_case form of the
10	C++ package, and the type name is the suffix after the first underscore:
11	
12	| C++ Class                      | Header                              | Rust Path                              |
13	|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
14	| \`gp_Pnt\`                       | \`gp_Pnt.hxx\`                       | \`gp::Pnt\`                             |
15	| \`BRepBuilderAPI_MakeEdge\`      | \`BRepBuilderAPI_MakeEdge.hxx\`       | \`b_rep_builder_api::MakeEdge\`          |
16	| \`BRepOffsetAPI_MakeThickSolid\` | \`BRepOffsetAPI_MakeThickSolid.hxx\`  | \`b_rep_offset_api::MakeThickSolid\`     |
17	| \`BRepOffsetSimple_Status\`      | \`BRepOffset_MakeSimpleOffset.hxx\`   | \`b_rep_offset::SimpleStatus\`           |
18	| \`TopoDS_Shape\`                 | \`TopoDS_Shape.hxx\`                  | \`topo_ds::Shape\`                       |
19	| \`Geom_CylindricalSurface\`      | \`Geom_CylindricalSurface.hxx\`      | \`geom::CylindricalSurface\`            |
20	| \`Geom2d_Ellipse\`               | \`Geom2d_Ellipse.hxx\`               | \`geom2d::Ellipse\`                     |
21	| \`GC_MakeSegment\`               | \`GC_MakeSegment.hxx\`               | \`gc::MakeSegment\`                     |
22	
23	## Constructors
24	
25	C++ constructors map to \`new_*\` associated functions. The suffix encodes the
26	parameter types to disambiguate overloads:
27	
28	\`\`\`cpp
29	// C++
30	gp_Pnt aPnt(1.0, 2.0, 3.0);
31	GC_MakeSegment aSegment(aPnt1, aPnt2);
32	BRepBuilderAPI_MakeWire aWire(edge1, edge2, edge3);
33	\`\`\`
34	
35	\`\`\`rust
36	// Rust
37	let a_pnt = gp::Pnt::new_real3(1.0, 2.0, 3.0);
38	let a_segment = gc::MakeSegment::new_pnt2(&a_pnt1, &a_pnt2);
39	let mut a_wire = b_rep_builder_api::MakeWire::new_edge3(
40	    edge1.edge(),
41	    edge2.edge(),
42	    edge3.edge(),
43	);
44	\`\`\`
45	
46	The default (no-argument) constructor is just \`::new()\`:
47	
48	\`\`\`rust
49	let mut trsf = gp::Trsf::new();
50	let mut compound = topo_ds::Compound::new();
51	\`\`\`
52	
53	### Constructors with Default Arguments
54	
55	C++ constructors with trailing default parameters have convenience wrappers
56	that omit the defaulted arguments. You can use either the short or full form:
57	
58	\`\`\`cpp
59	// C++: BRepBuilderAPI_Transform(shape, trsf)  — copy defaults to false
60	BRepBuilderAPI_Transform aBRepTrsf(aShape, aTrsf);
61	\`\`\`
62	
63	\`\`\`rust
64	// Rust: convenience wrapper fills in defaults
65	let mut brep_transform = b_rep_builder_api::Transform::new_shape_trsf(
66	    wire.shape(), &trsf,
67	);
68	
69	// Or explicitly pass all args
70	let mut brep_transform = b_rep_builder_api::Transform::new_shape_trsf_bool2(
71	    wire.shape(), &trsf, false, false,
72	);
73	\`\`\`
74	
75	## Ownership
76	
77	All OCCT objects are returned as \`OwnedPtr<T>\`. This type implements
78	\`Deref<Target=T>\` and \`DerefMut<Target=T>\`, so methods on \`T\` can be called
79	directly without any special pinning:
80	
81	\`\`\`rust
82	let mut trsf = gp::Trsf::new();
83	trsf.set_mirror_ax1(&x_axis);  // DerefMut provides &mut Self
84	
85	let name = type_obj.name();  // Deref provides &Self
86	\`\`\`
87	
88	Methods that return references to internal state (like \`.shape()\`, \`.wire()\`,
89	\`.edge()\`, \`.face()\`) work through auto-deref:
90	
91	\`\`\`rust
92	let shape = body.shape();     // returns &TopoDS_Shape
93	let wire = make_wire.wire();  // returns &TopoDS_Wire
94	\`\`\`
95	
96	## Handle Types (Reference-Counted Smart Pointers)
97	
98	OCCT's \`Handle(T)\` maps to \`OwnedPtr<HandleT>\` in Rust (e.g.,
99	\`Handle(Geom_Curve)\` → \`OwnedPtr<HandleGeomCurve>\`).
100	
101	### Creating Handles
102	
103	\`to_handle()\` is an associated function (not a method) that consumes an
104	\`OwnedPtr<T>\` and returns \`OwnedPtr<HandleT>\`. This is because
105	\`self: OwnedPtr<Self>\` receivers require Rust's unstable \`arbitrary_self_types\`
106	feature.
107	
108	\`\`\`cpp
109	// C++: Handle is created implicitly with new
110	Handle(Geom_CylindricalSurface) aCyl = new Geom_CylindricalSurface(anAx3, r);
111	\`\`\`
112	
113	\`\`\`rust
114	// Rust: create object, then convert to handle (consumes the object)
115	let cyl = geom::CylindricalSurface::new_ax3_real(&an_ax3, radius);
116	let handle_cyl = geom::CylindricalSurface::to_handle(cyl);
117	// \`cyl\` is now consumed and cannot be used
118	\`\`\`
119	
120	### Cloning Handles
121	
122	Handle types implement \`Clone\` via the \`CppCopyable\` trait. Cloning a handle
123	increments the reference count — both handles point to the same underlying
124	object:
125	
126	\`\`\`rust
127	let handle_clone = handle_cyl.clone();
128	// handle_cyl and handle_clone both reference the same Geom_CylindricalSurface
129	\`\`\`
130	
131	This also works with methods that return \`&HandleT\` — use \`.to_owned()\`
132	(from the \`ToOwned\` trait) to create an independently-owned \`OwnedPtr\`:
133	
134	\`\`\`rust
135	let curve_ref: &HandleGeomCurve = geom_api_obj.line(1);  // borrowed
136	let owned_curve = curve_ref.to_owned();                    // OwnedPtr<HandleGeomCurve>
137	\`\`\`
138	
139	### Handle Upcasting
140	
141	Use \`to_handle_*()\` methods to upcast handles in the inheritance hierarchy:
142	
143	\`\`\`rust
144	// HandleGeomCylindricalSurface → HandleGeomSurface
145	let handle_surface = handle_cyl.to_handle_surface();
146	
147	// HandleGeomTrimmedCurve → HandleGeomCurve
148	let handle_curve = segment.value().to_handle_curve();
149	\`\`\`
150	
151	These are \`&self\` methods, so the original handle remains usable.
152	
153	### Handle Dereferencing
154	
155	Use \`.get()\` to access the underlying object through a Handle:
156	
157	\`\`\`cpp
158	// C++: Handle auto-dereferences
159	gp_Pnt2d p = anEllipseHandle->Value(0);
160	\`\`\`
161	
162	\`\`\`rust
163	// Rust: explicit .get() dereference
164	let p = handle_ellipse.get().value(0.0);
165	\`\`\`
166	
167	### Null Handle Checking
168	
169	Some OCCT methods return null Handles (e.g., \`BRep_Tool::Triangulation\` when a
170	face has no triangulation). Use \`.is_null()\` to check before dereferencing:
171	
172	\`\`\`cpp
173	// C++: Handle has IsNull()
174	Handle(Poly_Triangulation) tri = BRep_Tool::Triangulation(face, loc);
175	if (tri.IsNull()) { continue; }
176	\`\`\`
177	
178	\`\`\`rust
179	// Rust: .is_null() method on Handle types
180	let tri_handle = b_rep::Tool::triangulation(face, &mut location, 0);
181	if tri_handle.is_null() {
182	    continue;
183	}
184	let tri = tri_handle.get();
185	\`\`\`
186	
187	Calling \`.get()\` on a null Handle will panic.
188	
189	
190	### Handle Downcasting
191	
192	Handle downcasting (e.g., \`Handle(Geom_Surface)\` → \`Handle(Geom_Plane)\`) is
193	supported via generated \`downcast_to_*()\` methods on Handle types. These use
194	OCCT's \`Handle::DownCast\` internally, which performs runtime type checking.
195	
196	\`\`\`rust
197	let surface = b_rep::Tool::surface_face(face);
198	
199	// Try to downcast HandleGeomSurface to HandleGeomPlane
200	if let Some(plane_handle) = surface.downcast_to_plane() {
201	    let plane = plane_handle.get();
202	    let location = plane.location();
203	    // ...
204	}
205	\`\`\`
206	
207	Downcasts are generated from each base Handle type to all of its concrete
208	(non-abstract) descendants. The methods return \`Option<OwnedPtr<HandleDerived>>\`,
209	so no unsafe code is needed.
210	
211	## Enums
212	
213	**Most enum parameters use typed Rust enums directly.** You
214	pass and receive Rust enum values:
215	
216	\`\`\`cpp
217	// C++
218	TopExp_Explorer explorer(shape, TopAbs_EDGE, TopAbs_SHAPE);
219	BRepFilletAPI_MakeFillet fillet(shape, ChFi3d_Rational);
220	\`\`\`
221	
222	\`\`\`rust
223	// Rust — pass enum values directly
224	let explorer = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
225	    shape,
226	    top_abs::ShapeEnum::Edge,
227	    top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
228	);
229	let fillet = b_rep_fillet_api::MakeFillet::new_shape_filletshape(
230	    shape,
231	    ch_fi3d::FilletShape::Rational,
232	);
233	\`\`\`
234	
235	Return values are also typed enums:
236	
237	\`\`\`rust
238	let orientation: top_abs::Orientation = shape.orientation();
239	let curve_type: geom_abs::CurveType = curve.get_type();
240	\`\`\`
241	
242	**Bitset enums** (those used as bitmasks, e.g. names containing "Flag" or
243	"Mask", or enums whose values are powers of 2) remain as \`i32\` and still
244	require manual conversion:
245	
246	\`\`\`rust
247	// Bitset enums still use i32
248	some_function(my_flags as i32);
249	\`\`\`
250	
251	Convert from \`i32\` back to enum with \`TryFrom\`:
252	
253	\`\`\`rust
254	let shape_enum = top_abs::ShapeEnum::try_from(raw_i32)
255	    .expect("Invalid ShapeEnum value");
256	\`\`\`
257	
258	## Collections
259	
260	Collection types like \`TopTools_ListOfShape\` have \`new()\`, \`append()\`,
261	\`prepend()\`, \`size()\`, and \`clear()\` methods:
262	
263	\`\`\`cpp
264	// C++
265	TopTools_ListOfShape aList;
266	aList.Append(aFace);
267	\`\`\`
268	
269	\`\`\`rust
270	// Rust
271	let mut faces = top_tools::ListOfShape::new();
272	faces.append(a_face.as_shape());
273	\`\`\`
274	
275	\`TopTools_IndexedMapOfShape\` provides deduplicated, indexed access to shapes.
276	Use \`top_exp::map_shapes()\` to populate it with sub-shapes of a given type:
277	
278	\`\`\`cpp
279	// C++
280	TopTools_IndexedMapOfShape vertexMap;
281	TopExp::MapShapes(shape, TopAbs_VERTEX, vertexMap);
282	for (int i = 1; i <= vertexMap.Extent(); ++i) {
283	    const TopoDS_Vertex& v = TopoDS::Vertex(vertexMap.FindKey(i));
284	}
285	\`\`\`
286	
287	\`\`\`rust
288	// Rust
289	let mut vertex_map = top_tools::IndexedMapOfShape::new();
290	top_exp::map_shapes(shape, top_abs::ShapeEnum::Vertex, &mut *vertex_map);
291	for i in 1..=vertex_map.size() {
292	    let v = unsafe { &*topo_ds::vertex(vertex_map.find_key(i)) };
293	}
294	\`\`\`
295	
296	Note: prefer \`map_shapes\` over \`TopExp_Explorer\` when you need unique shapes.
297	\`Explorer\` may visit the same vertex/edge multiple times (once per adjacent
298	element), which can cause issues with operations like \`MakeFillet2d::AddFillet\`
299	that must receive each vertex exactly once.
300	
301	## TopoDS Shape Casting
302	
303	OCCT uses free functions to downcast \`TopoDS_Shape\` references into specific
304	subtypes. These are available as module-level functions in \`topo_ds\`. They are
305	\`unsafe extern "C"\` functions that take/return raw pointers:
306	
307	\`\`\`cpp
308	// C++
309	const TopoDS_Edge& anEdge = TopoDS::Edge(aShape);
310	const TopoDS_Wire& aWire = TopoDS::Wire(aShape);
311	const TopoDS_Face& aFace = TopoDS::Face(aShape);
312	\`\`\`
313	
314	\`\`\`rust
315	// Rust — requires unsafe, returns raw pointer that must be dereferenced
316	let an_edge = unsafe { &*topo_ds::edge(a_shape) };     // &TopoDS_Edge
317	let a_wire = unsafe { &*topo_ds::wire(a_shape) };       // &TopoDS_Wire
318	let a_face = unsafe { &*topo_ds::face(a_shape) };       // &TopoDS_Face
319	\`\`\`
320	
321	When passing an \`OwnedPtr<T>\` to these functions, use \`.as_ptr()\` since
322	\`&OwnedPtr<T>\` does NOT auto-coerce to \`*const T\`:
323	
324	\`\`\`rust
325	let shape: OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Shape> = /* ... */;
326	let solid = unsafe { &*topo_ds::solid(shape.as_ptr()) };  // .as_ptr() needed
327	\`\`\`
328	
329	When passing \`&Shape\` (a regular reference from a method return), it auto-coerces:
330	
331	\`\`\`rust
332	let shape_ref: &topo_ds::Shape = make_solid.shape();
333	let solid = unsafe { &*topo_ds::solid(shape_ref) };       // &T → *const T works
334	\`\`\`
335	
336	## Shape Inheritance (as_shape / as_shape_mut)
337	
338	TopoDS subtypes (Edge, Wire, Face, Solid, Compound, etc.) inherit from
339	\`TopoDS_Shape\`. Use \`as_shape()\` and \`as_shape_mut()\` to get a Shape reference:
340	
341	\`\`\`rust
342	let shape_ref: &topo_ds::Shape = compound.as_shape();
343	let shape_mut: &mut topo_ds::Shape = compound.as_shape_mut();
344	\`\`\`
345	
346	## Static Methods
347	
348	C++ static methods become associated functions on the Rust type:
349	
350	\`\`\`cpp
351	// C++
352	Handle(Geom_Surface) aSurf = BRep_Tool::Surface(aFace);
353	\`\`\`
354	
355	\`\`\`rust
356	// Rust
357	let a_surf = b_rep::Tool::surface_face(a_face);
358	\`\`\`
359	
360	## Utility Class Functions
361	
362	OCCT "utility classes" (classes with only static methods and no instance
363	methods) are automatically converted to module-level free functions:
364	
365	\`\`\`cpp
366	// C++
367	BRepLib::BuildCurves3d(aWire);
368	BRepBndLib::Add(aShape, aBox, useTriangulation);
369	BRepGProp::SurfaceProperties(aShape, props);
370	gp_Pnt origin = gp::Origin();
371	gp_Ax1 ox = gp::OX();
372	\`\`\`
373	
374	\`\`\`rust
375	// Rust
376	b_rep_lib::build_curves3d(a_wire.as_shape());
377	unsafe { b_rep_bnd_lib::add(a_shape, &mut *a_box, true) };
378	unsafe { b_rep_g_prop::surface_properties(a_shape, &mut *props, false, false) };
379	let origin = gp::origin();
380	let ox = gp::ox();
381	\`\`\`
382	
383	Note: Raw re-exported free functions from \`ffi.rs\` (like \`b_rep_bnd_lib::add\`,
384	\`b_rep_g_prop::surface_properties\`) are \`unsafe extern "C"\`. When passing
385	\`OwnedPtr<T>\` to \`*mut T\` parameters, use \`&mut *owned_ptr\` to get \`&mut T\`
386	which then auto-coerces to \`*mut T\`.
387	
388	## Default-Argument Convenience Constructors
389	
390	When a C++ constructor has trailing parameters with default values, convenience
391	wrappers are generated that omit those parameters:
392	
393	\`\`\`cpp
394	// C++ — defaults: Copy=Standard_False, CopyMesh=Standard_False
395	BRepBuilderAPI_Transform T(S, trsf);  // uses defaults
396	BRepBuilderAPI_Transform T(S, trsf, true, false);  // explicit
397	\`\`\`
398	
399	\`\`\`rust
400	// Rust
401	let t = b_rep_builder_api::Transform::new_shape_trsf(&s, &trsf);    // uses defaults
402	let t = b_rep_builder_api::Transform::new_shape_trsf_bool2(&s, &trsf, true, false);  // explicit
403	\`\`\`
404	
405	## Message_ProgressRange
406	
407	Several OCCT operations (Boolean operations, meshing, thick solid) require a
408	\`Message_ProgressRange\` parameter that doesn't exist in older tutorials. Create
409	a default one:
410	
411	\`\`\`rust
412	let progress = message::ProgressRange::new();
413	let mut fuse = b_rep_algo_api::Fuse::new_shape2_progressrange(
414	    body_shape, cylinder_shape, &progress,
415	);
416	\`\`\`
417	
418	## Complete Translation Example
419	
420	Here is a side-by-side comparison of a typical sequence:
421	
422	\`\`\`cpp
423	// C++ — Create a cylinder and fuse it with a body
424	gp_Ax2 neckAx2(gp_Pnt(0, 0, height), gp::DZ());
425	BRepPrimAPI_MakeCylinder MKCyl(neckAx2, neckR, neckH);
426	BRepAlgoAPI_Fuse mkFuse(myBody, MKCyl.Shape());
427	TopoDS_Shape myBody = mkFuse.Shape();
428	\`\`\`
429	
430	\`\`\`rust
431	// Rust
432	let neck_ax2 = gp::Ax2::new_pnt_dir(
433	    &gp::Pnt::new_real3(0.0, 0.0, height),
434	    &gp::dz(),
435	);
436	let mut mk_cyl = b_rep_prim_api::MakeCylinder::new_ax2_real2(
437	    &neck_ax2, neck_r, neck_h,
438	);
439	let progress = message::ProgressRange::new();
440	let mut mk_fuse = b_rep_algo_api::Fuse::new_shape2_progressrange(
441	    my_body, mk_cyl.shape(), &progress,
442	);
443	let my_body = mk_fuse.shape();
444	\`\`\`
445	
446	## Known Limitations
447	
448	- **\`to_handle()\` is a static function**, not a method — use
449	  \`Type::to_handle(obj)\` instead of \`obj.to_handle()\`. This is due to Rust's
450	  \`arbitrary_self_types\` feature not being stable yet.
451	- **\`OwnedPtr<T>\` vs \`*const T\` coercion** — \`&OwnedPtr<T>\` does NOT
452	  auto-coerce to \`*const T\`. When calling raw FFI free functions that take
453	  \`*const T\`, use \`owned_ptr.as_ptr()\` to get \`*const T\`, or \`&*owned_ptr\`
454	  to get \`&T\` (which then auto-coerces). For \`*mut T\`, use
455	  \`owned_ptr.as_mut_ptr()\` or \`&mut *owned_ptr\`.
456	- **Bitset/flag enums remain \`i32\`** — most enum parameters now use typed Rust
457	  enums, but enums used as bitmasks (names containing "Flag" or "Mask", or
458	  values that are powers of 2) are still \`i32\`.
459	- **\`&mut\` enum out-params use typed enum references** — when a method has an
460	  enum output parameter (e.g., \`GeomAbs_Shape& val\`), the Rust signature uses
461	  a typed enum reference (e.g., \`&mut crate::geom_abs::Shape\`). The binding
462	  handles the \`i32\` ↔ enum conversion automatically.
463	
464	## RTTI Type Identification
465	
466	All classes inheriting from \`Standard_Transient\` have a \`get_type_name()\`
467	method that returns the C++ class name as a \`String\`. This is useful for
468	debugging and RTTI type identification:
469	
470	\`\`\`rust
471	let surface_handle = b_rep::Tool::surface_face(face);
472	let type_name = surface_handle.get().get_type_name();
473	println!("Surface type: {}", type_name); // e.g., "Geom_Plane"
474	\`\`\`
475	
476	For type-checked downcasting, prefer the \`downcast_to_*()\` methods on Handle
477	types (see the Handle Downcasting section above).
478	
479	## Inherited Methods on TopoDS Subtypes
480	
481	Most \`TopoDS_Shape\` methods are available directly on subtypes (\`Face\`, \`Edge\`,
482	\`Wire\`, \`Shell\`, \`Solid\`, \`Compound\`) as inherited methods — no \`as_shape()\`
483	needed:
484	
485	\`\`\`rust
486	// These work directly on Face, Edge, etc.
487	face.is_null()
488	face.location()
489	face.move_(&location, false)
490	face.reverse()
491	face.reversed()
492	face.nb_children()
493	face.is_same(other_shape)
494	face.orientation()           // top_abs::Orientation
495	face.shape_type()            // top_abs::ShapeEnum
496	face.oriented(0)             // returns OwnedPtr<Shape>
497	face.compose(0)              // mutating: compose orientation
498	face.composed(0)             // returns OwnedPtr<Shape>
499	// ... and: nullify, located, t_shape, free, locked, modified, checked,
500	//          orientable, closed, infinite, convex, moved, complement,
501	//          complemented, is_partner, is_equal, is_not_equal, empty_copy,
502	//          empty_copied, orientation_orientation
503	\`\`\`
504	
505	## Handle Chaining for Law Functions
506	
507	Some OCCT patterns require chaining through multiple handle conversions:
508	
509	\`\`\`rust
510	// Create a Law_Interpol, convert to Handle(Law_Interpol), then to Handle(Law_Function)
511	let mut interpol = law::Interpol::new();
512	interpol.set_array1ofpnt2d_bool(&array, false);
513	let handle = law::Interpol::to_handle(interpol);  // Handle(Law_Interpol)
514	let law_handle = handle.to_handle_function();       // Handle(Law_Function)
515	\`\`\`
516	
517	## OCCT 8.0.0 deprecated backward-compatibility aliases
518	
519	OCCT 8.0.0 moved ~970 backward-compat typedef headers into
520	\`OCCT/src/Deprecated/NCollectionAliases/\` (e.g. \`TColgp_HArray1OfPnt.hxx\` is now
521	just \`typedef NCollection_HArray1<gp_Pnt> TColgp_HArray1OfPnt;\`). OCCT's own 8.0 API
522	has already pivoted to the canonical \`NCollection_...<T>\` template names — method
523	signatures use \`NCollection_List<TopoDS_Shape>\` in ~190 headers vs. \`TopTools_ListOfShape\`
524	in only ~9 — and the deprecation messages explicitly say "use \`NCollection_List<TopoDS_Shape>\`
525	directly."
526	
527	The binding generator excludes these alias headers automatically via
528	\`exclude_deprecated_headers\` (config flag, default true), which matches the standard
529	banner comment \`"Deprecated typedef for backward compatibility"\` in header content
530	(see \`config::is_deprecated_alias_header\`). This replaces the old approach of listing
531	each alias header individually in \`exclude_headers\`. \`Standard_Macro.hxx\` (defines the
532	macro) and \`NCollection_Vector.hxx\` (a template alias, not a concrete instantiation) are
533	intentionally *not* matched.
534	
535	### KNOWN GAP — collections must be pivoted to canonical names (next task)
536	
537	### DONE — collections auto-discovered under canonical names
538	
539	\`codegen/collections.rs\` no longer hardcodes deprecated alias names. Instead:
540	
541	- \`collect_collection_spellings()\` scans all class/function signatures for referenced
542	  \`NCollection_*<...>\` template spellings (the exact spellings OCCT 8.0 uses, so map
543	  hasher args are captured correctly).
544	- \`parse_canonical_collection(spelling)\` derives the \`CollectionKind\`, element/key/value
545	  types, the canonical mangled FFI name via \`config::template_alias_name\`
546	  (\`NCollection_List<TopoDS_Shape>\` → \`NCollection_List_TopoDS_Shape\`), and module
547	  \`n_collection\`.
548	- \`discover_collections()\` (called from \`main.rs\`, replacing \`all_known_collections\`)
549	  materializes a collection for each spelling whose element/value types are bindable
550	  (a parsed class or a primitive), plus a small curated \`seed_collection_spellings()\`.
551	- \`generate_cpp_collection\` emits a C++ \`typedef <spelling> <mangled>;\` bridge, so the
552	  existing per-kind generation keeps using the mangled name; \`collect_collection_headers\`
553	  includes the \`NCollection_<Kind>.hxx\` template header + element headers.
554	- Canonical names go into \`collection_type_names\`, so \`generate_opaque_declarations\`
555	  skips them (no duplicate opaque struct/destructor).
556	
557	Result: \`Array1_gp_Pnt\`, \`List_TopoDS_Shape\`, \`DataMap_*\`, etc. re-exported from
558	\`n_collection\` with full method sets, and method signatures reference the *same*
559	canonical types. \`opencascade-sys\` builds/links; all 22 generator tests pass.
560	
561	### DONE — HArray1/HSequence handle collections (option (a))
562	
563	\`discover_collections\` now materializes handle kinds too. Ownership split:
564	- The **collection** owns the base type, element methods (\`new_int2\`, \`set_value\`, …),
565	  the destructor, and \`to_handle\` (C++ wrapper in \`generate_cpp_collection\` guarded by
566	  \`is_handle()\`; Rust FFI decl + \`to_handle\` method emitted for handle kinds).
567	- The \`template_instantiations\` entries in \`bindings.toml\` are **kept** — they register
568	  the instantiation as handle-able *at parse time* (so \`Handle(NCollection_HArray1<gp_Pnt>)\`
569	  parameters resolve, e.g. the \`GeomAPI_Interpolate\` ctor) and produce the handle *type*
570	  + machinery. Fully dropping them would require driving parse-time handle-ability from
571	  the codegen-time collection pass, which has ordering constraints — retaining them is the
572	  clean split.
573	- Duplicate-destructor conflict avoided: \`main.rs\` no longer adds a template-instantiation
574	  alias to \`extra_typedef_names\` when it is also a collection type (the collection owns the
575	  destructor).
576	
577	Result: \`n_collection::HArray1_gp_Pnt\` / \`HSequence_TopoDS_Shape\` have full method sets +
578	\`to_handle\`; the \`GeomAPI_Interpolate\` ctor is generated (was skipped). Handle types use the
579	\`Handle_<C++name>\` scheme (\`Handle_NCollection_HArray1_gp_Pnt\`). opencascade-sys builds/links;
580	22 generator tests pass.
581	
582	### DONE — high-level \`opencascade\` crate ported
583	
584	The \`opencascade\` crate and all in-repo examples build against OCCT 8.0. Full workspace
585	\`cargo build\` + \`cargo test\` are green (golden STEP files regenerated for 8.0 — the only
586	diff was the \`Open CASCADE ... 7.9\` → \`8.0\` version string in \`PRODUCT\` entities, plus
587	~1e-16 floating-point noise absorbed by the golden comparison's numeric tolerance).
588	
589	## Porting a client of older opencascade-rs to the OCCT 8.0 bindings
590	
591	If you have downstream Rust code written against the pre-8.0 bindings, here are the
592	high-level, client-visible changes to expect (all mechanical; the compiler will point you
593	at each site):
594	
595	### 1. Collections moved to canonical \`n_collection::\` names
596	OCCT 8.0 deprecated the \`TColgp_*\` / \`TColStd_*\` / \`TopTools_*\` collection aliases and
597	uses the canonical \`NCollection_*<T>\` templates directly. The bindings follow suit — every
598	collection now lives in the \`n_collection\` module named after the template + element:
599	
600	| Old | New |
601	|-----|-----|
602	| \`t_colgp::Array1OfPnt\` | \`n_collection::Array1_gp_Pnt\` |
603	| \`t_colgp::Array2OfPnt\` | \`n_collection::Array2_gp_Pnt\` |
604	| \`t_colgp::Array1OfPnt2d\` | \`n_collection::Array1_gp_Pnt2d\` |
605	| \`t_col_std::Array1OfReal\` | \`n_collection::Array1_double\` |
606	| \`top_tools::ListOfShape\` | \`n_collection::List_TopoDS_Shape\` |
607	| \`top_tools::SequenceOfShape\` | \`n_collection::Sequence_TopoDS_Shape\` |
608	| \`top_tools::IndexedMapOfShape\` | \`n_collection::IndexedMap_TopoDS_Shape\` |
609	
610	Shape-keyed maps carry the hasher in their name, e.g. a \`TopExp::MapShapes\` out-parameter is
611	\`n_collection::IndexedMap_TopoDS_Shape_TopTools_ShapeMapHasher\` (not the bare \`IndexedMap_TopoDS_Shape\`).
612	Collections of scalars are supported too (\`List_int\`, \`Map_int\`, \`Sequence_double\`,
613	\`DataMap_TopoDS_Shape_int\`, …); scalar map lookups return \`Option<T>\` by value.
614	
615	### 2. Handle types use the \`Handle_<C++name>\` scheme
616	\`HandleGeomCurve\` → \`Handle_Geom_Curve\`, \`HandleGeomSurface\` → \`Handle_Geom_Surface\`,
617	\`HandleLawFunction\` → \`Handle_Law_Function\`, etc. (matches OCCT's own classic \`Handle_X\`
618	spelling). Handle *methods* (\`get\`, \`get_mut\`, \`is_null\`, \`to_handle_*\`, \`downcast_to_*\`)
619	are unchanged.
620	
621	### 3. \`HArray1\`/\`HSequence\` are collections now
622	Formerly stand-alone classes (\`t_colgp::HArray1OfPnt\`), they are \`n_collection::HArray1_gp_Pnt\`
623	/ \`HSequence_TopoDS_Shape\`, etc. Because \`NCollection_HArray1<T>\` *is* an \`NCollection_Array1<T>\`,
624	call element methods directly: \`array.change_array1().set_value(i, v)\` becomes
625	\`array.set_value(i, v)\`. \`to_handle(owned)\` and (on the resulting handle) \`get()\`/\`get_mut()\`
626	work as before.
627	
628	### 4. Overloaded method/ctor suffixes follow the new element names
629	Suffixes are derived from the canonical element type, so:
630	\`BezierCurve::new_array1ofpnt\` → \`new_array1_gp_pnt\`,
631	\`BezierSurface::new_array2ofpnt\` → \`new_array2_gp_pnt\`,
632	\`MakeFillet::add_array1ofpnt2d_edge\` → \`add_array1_gp_pnt2d_edge\`,
633	\`Interpol::set_array1ofpnt2d_bool\` → \`set_array1_gp_pnt2d_bool\`,
634	\`GeomAPI_Interpolate::new_handletcolgpharray1ofpnt_bool_real\` →
635	\`new_handlencollectionharray1gppnt_bool_real\`.
636	
637	### 5. Deprecated OCCT symbols are gone — use the 8.0 replacement
638	Deprecated headers aren't bound at all (see the "OCCT 8.0.0 deprecated ..." section above).
639	Notable API relocations/signature changes encountered:
640	- \`GCE2d_MakeSegment\` (and other \`GCE2d_*\` builders) → the consolidated \`GC_*\` equivalents,
641	  e.g. \`gce2d::MakeSegment\` → \`gc::MakeSegment2d\` (value returns \`Handle_Geom2d_TrimmedCurve\`).
642	- \`ShapeAnalysis_FreeBounds::connect_edges_to_wires\` now **returns** the wire
643	  \`Handle_NCollection_HSequence_TopoDS_Shape\` and takes 3 args \`(edges, tol, shared)\`
644	  (the wires out-parameter was removed).
645	- \`StlAPI_Writer::write\` → \`write_shape_charptr_progressrange(shape, path, progress)\`.
646	- \`GeomAPI_Interpolate::load_vec2_bool\` → \`load(initial_tangent, final_tangent, scale)\`.
647	
```
</details>

## Collections

Collection types like `TopTools_ListOfShape` have `new()`, `append()`,
`prepend()`, `size()`, and `clear()` methods:

```cpp
// C++
TopTools_ListOfShape aList;
aList.Append(aFace);
```

```rust
// Rust
let mut faces = top_tools::ListOfShape::new();
faces.append(a_face.as_shape());
```

`TopTools_IndexedMapOfShape` provides deduplicated, indexed access to shapes.
Use `top_exp::map_shapes()` to populate it with sub-shapes of a given type:

```cpp
// C++
TopTools_IndexedMapOfShape vertexMap;
TopExp::MapShapes(shape, TopAbs_VERTEX, vertexMap);
for (int i = 1; i <= vertexMap.Extent(); ++i) {
    const TopoDS_Vertex& v = TopoDS::Vertex(vertexMap.FindKey(i));
}
```

```rust
// Rust
let mut vertex_map = top_tools::IndexedMapOfShape::new();
top_exp::map_shapes(shape, top_abs::ShapeEnum::Vertex, &mut *vertex_map);
for i in 1..=vertex_map.size() {
    let v = unsafe { &*topo_ds::vertex(vertex_map.find_key(i)) };
}
```

Note: prefer `map_shapes` over `TopExp_Explorer` when you need unique shapes.
````

**After:**
````markdown
## Collections

OCCT's collections are the `NCollection_*<T>` templates (`NCollection_List<TopoDS_Shape>`,
`NCollection_Array1<gp_Pnt>`, `NCollection_DataMap<...>`, …). Each instantiation is
re-exported in the `n_collection` module under a canonical name formed from the template
and its element type(s): `n_collection::List_TopoDS_Shape`, `n_collection::Array1_gp_Pnt`,
`n_collection::HArray1_gp_Pnt`, etc. Shape-keyed maps carry the hasher in their name
(`n_collection::IndexedMap_TopoDS_Shape_TopTools_ShapeMapHasher`). Scalar-element
collections are supported too (`List_int`, `Sequence_double`, `DataMap_TopoDS_Shape_int`);
their scalar accessors take/return the value by `&i32`/`Option<i32>` rather than a pointer.

List/sequence types have `new()`, `append()`, `prepend()`, `value()`, `size()`, and
`clear()`; `Array1`/`HArray1` add `new_int2()`, `value()`, `set_value()`; maps add
`add()`/`bind()`/`find()`/`contains()`/`find_key()`.

```cpp
// C++
NCollection_List<TopoDS_Shape> aList;
aList.Append(aFace);
```

```rust
// Rust
let mut faces = n_collection::List_TopoDS_Shape::new();
faces.append(a_face.as_shape());
```

`NCollection_IndexedMap` provides deduplicated, indexed access. Use `TopExp::MapShapes`
(a free function whose name encodes the exact map instantiation) to populate it with
sub-shapes of a given type:

```cpp
// C++
NCollection_IndexedMap<TopoDS_Shape, TopTools_ShapeMapHasher> vertexMap;
TopExp::MapShapes(shape, TopAbs_VERTEX, vertexMap);
for (int i = 1; i <= vertexMap.Extent(); ++i) {
    const TopoDS_Vertex& v = TopoDS::Vertex(vertexMap.FindKey(i));
}
```

```rust
// Rust
let mut vertex_map = n_collection::IndexedMap_TopoDS_Shape_TopTools_ShapeMapHasher::new();
top_exp::map_shapes_shape_shapeenum_indexedmap_topods_shape_toptools_shapemaphasher(
    shape, top_abs::ShapeEnum::Vertex, &mut vertex_map,
);
for i in 1..=vertex_map.size() {
    let v = unsafe { &*topo_ds::vertex(vertex_map.find_key(i)) };
}
```

Note: prefer `map_shapes` over `TopExp_Explorer` when you need unique shapes.
````
</details>
