```markdown
## OCCT 8.0.0 deprecated backward-compatibility aliases

OCCT 8.0.0 moved ~970 backward-compat typedef headers into
`OCCT/src/Deprecated/NCollectionAliases/` (e.g. `TColgp_HArray1OfPnt.hxx` is now
just `typedef NCollection_HArray1<gp_Pnt> TColgp_HArray1OfPnt;`). OCCT's own 8.0 API
has already pivoted to the canonical `NCollection_...<T>` template names — method
signatures use `NCollection_List<TopoDS_Shape>` in ~190 headers vs. `TopTools_ListOfShape`
in only ~9 — and the deprecation messages explicitly say "use `NCollection_List<TopoDS_Shape>`
directly."

The binding generator excludes these alias headers automatically via
`exclude_deprecated_headers` (config flag, default true), which matches the standard
banner comment `"Deprecated typedef for backward compatibility"` in header content
(see `config::is_deprecated_alias_header`). This replaces the old approach of listing
each alias header individually in `exclude_headers`. `Standard_Macro.hxx` (defines the
macro) and `NCollection_Vector.hxx` (a template alias, not a concrete instantiation) are
intentionally *not* matched.

### KNOWN GAP — collections must be pivoted to canonical names (next task)

### DONE — collections auto-discovered under canonical names

`codegen/collections.rs` no longer hardcodes deprecated alias names. Instead:

- `collect_collection_spellings()` scans all class/function signatures for referenced
  `NCollection_*<...>` template spellings (the exact spellings OCCT 8.0 uses, so map
  hasher args are captured correctly).
- `parse_canonical_collection(spelling)` derives the `CollectionKind`, element/key/value
  types, the canonical mangled FFI name via `config::template_alias_name`
  (`NCollection_List<TopoDS_Shape>` → `NCollection_List_TopoDS_Shape`), and module
  `n_collection`.
- `discover_collections()` (called from `main.rs`, replacing `all_known_collections`)
  materializes a collection for each spelling whose element/value types are bindable
  (a parsed class or a primitive), plus a small curated `seed_collection_spellings()`.
- `generate_cpp_collection` emits a C++ `typedef <spelling> <mangled>;` bridge, so the
  existing per-kind generation keeps using the mangled name; `collect_collection_headers`
  includes the `NCollection_<Kind>.hxx` template header + element headers.
- Canonical names go into `collection_type_names`, so `generate_opaque_declarations`
  skips them (no duplicate opaque struct/destructor).

Result: `Array1_gp_Pnt`, `List_TopoDS_Shape`, `DataMap_*`, etc. re-exported from
`n_collection` with full method sets, and method signatures reference the *same*
canonical types. `opencascade-sys` builds/links; all 22 generator tests pass.

### DONE — HArray1/HSequence handle collections (option (a))

`discover_collections` now materializes handle kinds too. Ownership split:
- The **collection** owns the base type, element methods (`new_int2`, `set_value`, …),
  the destructor, and `to_handle` (C++ wrapper in `generate_cpp_collection` guarded by
  `is_handle()`; Rust FFI decl + `to_handle` method emitted for handle kinds).
- The `template_instantiations` entries in `bindings.toml` are **kept** — they register
  the instantiation as handle-able *at parse time* (so `Handle(NCollection_HArray1<gp_Pnt>)`
  parameters resolve, e.g. the `GeomAPI_Interpolate` ctor) and produce the handle *type*
  + machinery. Fully dropping them would require driving parse-time handle-ability from
  the codegen-time collection pass, which has ordering constraints — retaining them is the
  clean split.
- Duplicate-destructor conflict avoided: `main.rs` no longer adds a template-instantiation
  alias to `extra_typedef_names` when it is also a collection type (the collection owns the
  destructor).

Result: `n_collection::HArray1_gp_Pnt` / `HSequence_TopoDS_Shape` have full method sets +
`to_handle`; the `GeomAPI_Interpolate` ctor is generated (was skipped). Handle types use the
`Handle_<C++name>` scheme (`Handle_NCollection_HArray1_gp_Pnt`). opencascade-sys builds/links;
22 generator tests pass.

### DONE — high-level `opencascade` crate ported

The `opencascade` crate and all in-repo examples build against OCCT 8.0. Full workspace
`cargo build` + `cargo test` are green (golden STEP files regenerated for 8.0 — the only
```

```
1	# opencascade-rs
2	
3	Comprehensive Rust FFI bindings to the [OpenCASCADE](https://dev.opencascade.org/) (OCCT) C++ CAD kernel, auto-generated from OCCT header files.
4	
5	## Background
6	
7	This is a fork of [bschwind/opencascade-rs](https://github.com/bschwind/opencascade-rs). The original project provides hand-written bindings covering a useful subset of OCCT, along with a higher-level \`opencascade\` crate and a WGPU-based viewer.
8	
9	I ([@sethml](https://github.com/sethml)) wanted to use Rust and OpenCASCADE to vibe-code an STL-to-STEP converter, and found that \`opencascade-sys\` was a good start but was missing many of the bindings I needed. Rather than hand-writing wrappers one by one, I built an automated binding generator that parses OCCT headers with libclang and emits a complete Rust FFI layer.
10	
11	This was an experiment in using LLM-assisted coding to bind nearly all of OCCT in a form that can be effectively used from Rust. I may have gone a bit overboard and accidentally recreated much of [bindgen](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-bindgen) — but specialized for OCCT's idioms (Handle smart pointers, NCollection iterators, inheritance upcasts, builder patterns, etc.).
12	
13	I started from bschwind's repo and kept all the existing examples working throughout — they served as an excellent way to verify that the new bindings didn't break anything. The higher-level \`opencascade\` crate and viewer are still fully functional.
14	
15	### Status
16	
17	- **8,700+ opaque types** and **164,000+ extern "C" functions** across **324 Rust modules**
18	- Parses **5,065 OCCT headers** with automatic dependency resolution
19	- Only **94 symbols** skipped (mostly platform-specific or external dependency types)
20	- **446 enums** generated as \`#[repr(i32)]\` Rust enums
21	- Passes unit tests and golden STEP-file tests on macOS and Linux
22	- Untested APIs likely have issues — this is a large surface area
23	
24	### What's next
25	
26	I'm honestly not sure how to proceed with releasing this to the greater Rust ecosystem. A few options:
27	- [@bschwind](https://github.com/bschwind) could pull these changes and repackage as a new crate version
28	- I could publish a separate crate (e.g., \`occt-sys\` or similar)
29	- Some other approach — suggestions welcome
30	
31	## Architecture
32	
33	The binding pipeline has three main pieces:
34	
35	1. **\`opencascade-binding-generator\`** — A Rust tool (~16k lines) that parses OCCT C++ headers with libclang, builds a symbol table, and generates both Rust FFI declarations and C++ wrapper functions. See [crates/opencascade-binding-generator/README.md](crates/opencascade-binding-generator/README.md) for full details on the architecture and generated API.
36	
37	2. **\`scripts/regenerate-bindings.sh\`** — Orchestrates the generator: builds it in release mode, cleans the output directory, and runs it against the TOML configuration.
38	
39	3. **\`opencascade-sys\`** — The generated crate. Contains \`generated/ffi.rs\` (a single \`extern "C"\` block with all types and functions), \`generated/wrappers.cpp\` (C++ glue code), and 324 per-module re-export files providing ergonomic short names.
40	
41	Configuration lives in \`crates/opencascade-sys/bindings.toml\`, which controls which OCCT modules/headers to include, symbol-level exclusions, type overrides, and template instantiations.
42	
43	### Porting from the old hand-written bindings
44	
45	If you're migrating code that used the previous \`opencascade-sys\` API, see [crates/opencascade-sys/PORTING.md](crates/opencascade-sys/PORTING.md) for a detailed guide on the API differences and migration patterns.
46	
47	## Dependencies
48	
49	* Rust toolchain (https://rustup.rs/)
50	* CMake (https://cmake.org/)
51	* A C++ compiler with C++11 support
52	* libclang (for regenerating bindings — not needed for just building)
53	
54	## Building
55	
56	The OCCT codebase is included as a git submodule. Clone the repo with the \`--recursive\` flag, or use \`git submodule update --init\` to fetch the submodule.
57	
58	\`\`\`bash
59	cargo build --release
60	\`\`\`
61	
62	The first build compiles OCCT from source via the \`builtin\` feature (enabled by default), which takes a while. Subsequent builds are fast — OCCT is only rebuilt if the submodule changes.
63	
64	### Using pre-installed OpenCASCADE
65	
66	If you have OCCT already installed via a package manager, you can dynamically link to it instead of building from source. Disable the \`builtin\` feature:
67	
68	\`\`\`bash
69	cargo build --no-default-features
70	\`\`\`
71	
72	or in your \`Cargo.toml\`:
73	
74	\`\`\`toml
75	[dependencies]
76	opencascade-sys = { version = "0.2", default-features = false }
77	\`\`\`
78	
79	If OCCT is installed in a non-standard location, set the \`DEP_OCCT_ROOT\` environment variable to the root directory (containing \`include/\` and \`lib/\` subdirectories).
80	
81	## Regenerating Bindings
82	
83	To regenerate the FFI layer after modifying the binding generator or \`bindings.toml\`:
84	
85	\`\`\`bash
86	# Regenerate bindings (requires libclang)
87	scripts/regenerate-bindings.sh
88	
89	# Build everything
90	cargo build
91	
92	# Run binding generator tests (requires libclang)
93	scripts/run-binding-generator-tests.sh
94	
95	# Run all other tests
96	cargo test --workspace --exclude opencascade-binding-generator
97	\`\`\`
98	
99	On macOS, the scripts automatically set \`DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH\` to find libclang from the Xcode toolchain. On Linux, ensure \`libclang\` is available (e.g., \`apt install libclang-dev\`).
100	
101	OCCT headers must be built first (\`cargo build -p occt-sys\` will do this). The generator reads them from \`target/OCCT/include/\`.
102	
103	## Run Examples
104	
105	### Higher Level
106	
107	The [higher level examples](./examples/src) use ergonomic Rust APIs built on top of \`opencascade-sys\`:
108	
109	\`\`\`bash
110	cargo run --release --example bottle
111	\`\`\`
112	
113	### Viewer Application
114	
115	There is an experimental WGPU-based viewer for visualizing models:
116	
117	\`\`\`bash

119	cargo run --release --bin viewer -- --example keycap
120	
121	# View a STEP file
122	cargo run --release --bin viewer -- --step-file SOME_FILE.step
123	\`\`\`
124	
125	### Lower Level (opencascade-sys)
126	
127	There are lower-level examples that directly call OpenCASCADE functions through the generated bindings:
128	
129	- [bottle.rs](./crates/opencascade-sys/examples/bottle.rs) — the classic OCCT bottle tutorial
130	- [simple.rs](./crates/opencascade-sys/examples/simple.rs) — basic shape creation
131	- [point_info_3d.rs](./crates/opencascade-sys/examples/point_info_3d.rs) — geometry queries
132	
133	### Golden Tests
134	
135	STEP-file golden tests verify that the examples produce consistent output:
136

138	cargo test --workspace --exclude opencascade-binding-generator
139	\`\`\`
140	
141	## Example Model Writer
142

144
```

```
1	# opencascade-binding-generator
2	
3	Automatically generates Rust \`extern "C"\` FFI bindings for the [OpenCASCADE](https://dev.opencascade.org/) C++ CAD kernel.
4	
5	Given a set of OCCT header files, the generator produces a complete Rust FFI layer: type declarations, method bindings, constructor wrappers, Handle smart pointer support, collection iterators, inheritance upcasts, and per-module re-exports with ergonomic short names.
6	
7	## Quick Start
8	
9	\`\`\`bash
10	# Regenerate all bindings (from repo root)
11	./scripts/regenerate-bindings.sh
12	\`\`\`
13	
14	This parses OCCT headers configured in \`bindings.toml\` (expanding with automatic dependency resolution), and writes generated code to \`crates/opencascade-sys/generated/\`.
15	
16	## CLI Usage
17	
18	\`\`\`bash
19	# Standard regeneration (from repo root):
20	./scripts/regenerate-bindings.sh
21	
22	# Manual invocation with TOML config:
23	cargo run -p opencascade-binding-generator -- \
24	    --config crates/opencascade-sys/bindings.toml \
25	    -I target/OCCT/include \
26	    -o crates/opencascade-sys/generated
27	
28	# Or with explicit header arguments (legacy):
29	cargo run -p opencascade-binding-generator -- \
30	    -I target/OCCT/include \
31	    -o crates/opencascade-sys/generated \
32	    target/OCCT/include/gp_Pnt.hxx target/OCCT/include/TopoDS_Shape.hxx ...
33	\`\`\`
34	
35	**Flags:**
36	- \`--config <file>\` — TOML configuration file specifying headers (recommended)
37	- \`--resolve-deps\` — Auto-include header dependencies (default: true)
38	- \`--dump-symbols\` — Dump symbol table for debugging
39	- \`--dry-run\` — Parse without generating
40	- \`-v, --verbose\` — Verbose output
41	- \`--module <name>\` — Filter to a specific module
42	
43	## Generated Public API
44	
45	Users interact with \`opencascade-sys\` through per-module re-exports. Each OCCT module (gp, TopoDS, BRepPrimAPI, etc.) becomes a Rust module with short type names and idiomatic method signatures.
46	
47	### Geometry Primitives
48	
49	Simple value types like points, vectors, and directions get constructors, accessors, and transformation methods. All methods go through extern "C" C++ wrappers. Methods that return class types by value return \`OwnedPtr<T>\`.
50	
51	\`\`\`rust
52	use opencascade_sys::gp::{Pnt, Vec, Dir, Ax1, Ax2, Trsf};
53	
54	// Constructors -- overloads distinguished by parameter type suffix
55	let origin = Pnt::new();                          // default constructor
56	let p = Pnt::new_real3(1.0, 2.0, 3.0);           // from coordinates
57	let p2 = Pnt::new_xyz(&xyz);                      // from XYZ
58	
59	// Direct accessors
60	let x: f64 = p.x();
61	let y: f64 = p.y();
62	p.set_x(10.0);
63	
64	// Transformations return OwnedPtr (by-value return needs C++ wrapper)
65	let mirrored: OwnedPtr<Pnt> = p.mirrored_pnt(&origin);
66	let rotated = p.rotated(&axis, std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2);
67	let transformed = p.transformed(&trsf);
68	
69	// Clone into a new OwnedPtr
70	let p_copy = p.clone();
71	
72	\`\`\`
73	
74	### Topology Types and Inheritance
75	
76	Topological shapes form an inheritance hierarchy: \`Shape\` is the base, with subtypes \`Vertex\`, \`Edge\`, \`Wire\`, \`Face\`, \`Shell\`, \`Solid\`, \`CompSolid\`, and \`Compound\`. Extern "C" FFI treats these as unrelated opaque types, so the generator produces explicit upcast methods (both const and mutable) and downcast free functions.
77	
78	\`\`\`rust
79	use opencascade_sys::topo_ds::{Shape, Edge, Face, Solid, Wire};
80	
81	// Upcasting -- every subtype can upcast to its ancestors
82	let edge = Edge::new();
83	let shape_ref: &Shape = edge.as_shape();                    // const upcast
84	let shape_mut: &mut Shape = edge.as_shape_mut();            // mutable upcast
85	
86	// Downcasting -- free functions in the topo_ds module
87	// (wraps OCCT's TopoDS::Edge(), TopoDS::Face(), etc.)
88	use opencascade_sys::topo_ds;
89	let edge: OwnedPtr<Edge> = topo_ds::edge(&some_shape);       // const
90	let face: OwnedPtr<Face> = topo_ds::face_mut(&mut shape);    // mutable
91	
92	// Copy semantics (TopoDS shapes are reference-counted internally)
93	let shape_copy = shape.clone();
94	
95	\`\`\`
96	
97	### Primitive Shape Construction (Builder Pattern)
98	
99	OCCT builder classes follow a pattern: construct with parameters, then extract the result by upcasting to \`MakeShape\` and calling \`shape()\`.
100	
101	\`\`\`rust
102	use opencascade_sys::gp::{Pnt, Ax2};
103	use opencascade_sys::b_rep_prim_api::{MakeBox, MakeSphere, MakeCylinder};
104	
105	// Overloaded constructors use parameter type suffixes
106	let mut make_box = MakeBox::new_real3(10.0, 20.0, 30.0);    // dx, dy, dz
107	let mut make_box = MakeBox::new_pnt_real3(&p, 10.0, 20.0, 30.0); // corner + size
108	let mut make_box = MakeBox::new_pnt2(&p1, &p2);             // two corners
109	let mut make_box = MakeBox::new_ax2_real3(&axes, 10.0, 20.0, 30.0); // local coords
110	
111	// Extract the result via mutable upcast to MakeShape
112	let make_shape = make_box.as_b_rep_builder_api_make_shape_mut();
113	let result: &TopoDS_Shape = make_shape.shape();
114	\`\`\`
115	
116	### Boolean Operations
117	
118	\`\`\`rust
119	use opencascade_sys::b_rep_algo_api::{Fuse, Cut, Common};
120	use opencascade_sys::message::ProgressRange;
121	
122	let progress = ProgressRange::new();
123	let mut fuse = Fuse::new_shape2_progressrange(&shape_a, &shape_b, &progress);
124	let make_shape = fuse.as_b_rep_builder_api_make_shape_mut();
125	let result = make_shape.shape();
126	\`\`\`
127	
128	### Static Methods
129	
130	C++ static methods become associated functions on the type. These go through free function wrappers in the extern "C" layer.
131	
132	\`\`\`rust
133	use opencascade_sys::b_rep_bnd_lib::BRepBndLib;
134	use opencascade_sys::bnd::Box;
135	
136	let mut bbox = Box::new();
137	// Static method: BRepBndLib::Add(shape, box, useTriangulation)
138	BRepBndLib::add(&shape, &mut bbox, true);
139	\`\`\`
140	
141	### Handle Types (Reference-Counted Smart Pointers)
142	
143	OCCT uses \`Handle<T>\` (an intrusive reference-counted pointer) for objects inheriting from \`Standard_Transient\`. The generator produces \`to_handle()\` to wrap an object, upcast methods to convert between Handle types in the inheritance hierarchy, \`Clone\` / \`ToOwned\` support for copying handles, and \`is_null()\` to check for null handles.
144	
145	\`\`\`rust
146	use opencascade_sys::geom::{BezierCurve, BSplineCurve};
147	
148	// Wrap a geometry object in a Handle
149	let curve: OwnedPtr<BezierCurve> = /* ... */;
150	let handle = BezierCurve::to_handle(curve);
151	// handle is OwnedPtr<HandleGeomBezierCurve>
152	
153	// Clone a handle (invokes C++ copy constructor)
154	let handle2 = handle.clone();
155	
156	// Check for null before dereferencing
157	if !handle.is_null() {
158	    let obj = handle.get();
159	}
160	
161	// Methods that return Handles
162	let copy = some_curve.copy();
163	// copy is OwnedPtr<HandleGeomGeometry>
164	\`\`\`
165	
166	
167	### const char* String Conversions
168	
169	Methods taking \`const char*\` accept \`&str\` in Rust; methods returning \`const char*\` return \`String\`. C++ wrappers pass through \`const char*\` directly.
170	
171	\`\`\`rust
172	use opencascade_sys::standard::Failure;
173	
174	// const char* return -> String
175	let msg: String = failure.get_message_string();
176	\`\`\`
177	
178	### Nullable Pointer Parameters
179	
180	Methods with \`T* param = NULL\` or \`const T* param = NULL\` use \`Option<&mut T>\` or \`Option<&T>\` in Rust. The C++ wrapper passes the raw pointer through — \`NULL\` for \`None\`, the underlying pointer for \`Some\`.
181	
182	\`\`\`rust
183	use opencascade_sys::bnd::OBB;
184	
185	// theListOfTolerances is Option<&TColStd_Array1OfReal> (const T* = NULL in C++)
186	obb.re_build(&points, Some(&tolerances), true);
187	obb.re_build(&points, None, false);  // pass NULL for tolerances
188	\`\`\`
189	
190	### Non-Nullable Class Pointer Parameters
191	
192	Methods with non-nullable \`const T*\` or \`T*\` parameters (where \`T\` is a known class type) are bound as \`&T\` or \`&mut T\` in Rust. The C++ wrapper passes the raw pointer through. This is safe because these parameters are documented as non-nullable in OCCT. Primitive pointer types (\`int*\`, \`double*\`) are NOT bound this way since they typically represent C-style arrays.
193	
194	\`\`\`rust
195	use opencascade_sys::adaptor3d::Surface;
196	
197	// const Adaptor3d_Surface* in C++ → &Surface in Rust
198	fn example(surface: &Surface) { /* ... */ }
199	\`\`\`
200	
201	### Fixed-Size Array Reference Parameters
202	
203	Methods taking fixed-size C++ arrays are now bound directly:
204	
205	- \`const T (&arr)[N]\` → \`&[T; N]\`
206	- \`T (&arr)[N]\` → \`&mut [T; N]\`
207	- \`const T arr[N]\` → \`&[T; N]\` (array parameter decays to pointer in C++)
208	- \`T arr[N]\` → \`&mut [T; N]\` (array parameter decays to pointer in C++)
209	
210	At the extern boundary, these lower to element pointers (\`*const T\` / \`*mut T\`). In C++ wrappers we reconstruct the array reference with \`reinterpret_cast\` back to \`T (*)[N]\` and pass \`*...\` into the original OCCT call.
211	
212	\`\`\`rust
213	use opencascade_sys::b_rep_mesh::MeshTool;
214	
215	let mut edges = [0_i32; 3];
216	mesh_tool.add_triangle(p1, p2, p3, &mut edges);
217	\`\`\`
218	
219	This unblocks APIs like \`BRepMesh_MeshTool::AddTriangle(Standard_Integer (&theEdges)[3])\` without hand-written bindings, and also fixed-size non-reference array parameters declared as \`T arr[N]\`.
220	
221	
222	### Class Pointer Returns
223	
224	Instance methods returning \`const T*\` or \`T*\` (where \`T\` is a known class type) are bound as \`Option<&T>\` or \`Option<&mut T>\` in Rust, with a null check. The C++ wrapper passes the raw pointer through — the Rust reexport checks for null and returns \`None\` or \`Some(&ref)\`. For const methods (\`&self\`), \`T*\` returns are downgraded to \`Option<&T>\` to avoid unsound \`&self -> &mut T\`. Static methods and free functions with class pointer returns are NOT bound this way (lifetime issues).
225	
226	\`\`\`rust
227	use opencascade_sys::geom::BSplineCurve;
228	
229	// const TColStd_Array1OfReal* in C++ → Option<&TColStd_Array1OfReal> in Rust
230	let weights: Option<&_> = curve.weights();  // None if null, Some(&array) otherwise
231	\`\`\`
232	
233	### Unsafe Reference Returns (Ambiguous Lifetimes)
234	
235	Some methods and free functions return a reference (\`&T\` or \`&mut T\`) while also taking reference parameters. In C++, the returned reference might borrow from \`self\`, from one of the parameters, or from neither (e.g., a global or class-static). Rust's lifetime elision rules assume the return borrows from \`self\` for methods, but this assumption may be incorrect — the return could actually borrow from a parameter, which might be dropped before \`self\`.
236	
237	The generator marks these methods as \`unsafe fn\` with a \`# Safety\` doc comment explaining the ambiguity. This applies to:
238	
239	- **Instance methods** returning \`&T\` or \`&mut T\` that also take reference parameters (other than \`self\`)
240	- **Free functions** returning a reference with 2+ reference parameters (no \`self\` to disambiguate)
241	
242	For free functions, explicit lifetime annotations (\`<'a>\`) tie all reference parameters and the return type together, since Rust's elision rules cannot resolve the ambiguity without \`self\`.
243	
244	\`\`\`rust
245	use opencascade_sys::message::Msg;
246	
247	// Method: returns &mut Msg, takes &str — could borrow from self or theString
248	let result: &mut Msg = unsafe { msg.arg_charptr("value") };
249	
250	// Free function: explicit lifetime <'a> ties parameters and return together
251	use opencascade_sys::bin_tools;
252	let stream: &mut OStream = unsafe { bin_tools::put_real(&mut os, &value) };
253	\`\`\`
254	
255	Methods that return references but take no reference parameters (other than \`self\`) are **safe** — Rust's lifetime elision correctly binds the return to \`self\`.
256	
257	### Collection Iterators
258	
259	OCCT collection types (NCollection_List, NCollection_Sequence, NCollection_IndexedMap, etc.) get Rust iterator support. Each collection has a C++ iterator wrapper struct and Rust \`Iterator\` trait impl.
260	
261	\`\`\`rust
262	use opencascade_sys::top_tools::ListOfShape;
263	use opencascade_sys::topo_ds::Shape;
264	
265	// Iterate over a list of shapes
266	for shape in list_of_shape.iter() {
267	    // shape: OwnedPtr<Shape>
268	    let x = shape.IsNull();
269	}
270	
271	// Build a list from an iterator
272	let list = ListOfShape::from_iter(shapes.iter());
273	\`\`\`
274	
275	### Enums
276	
277	OCCT enums are generated as \`#[repr(i32)]\` Rust enums with \`From<EnumType> for i32\` and \`TryFrom<i32> for EnumType\` conversions. Enum parameters in generated wrapper functions use typed Rust enums directly — the C++ wrapper handles the \`i32\` conversion at the FFI boundary.
278	
279	\`\`\`rust
280	use opencascade_sys::top_abs::ShapeEnum;
281	
282	let shape_type = ShapeEnum::Edge;
283	let raw: i32 = shape_type.into();
284	let back = ShapeEnum::try_from(raw).unwrap();
285	\`\`\`
286	
287	---
288	
289	## Architecture
290	
291	### FFI Architecture
292	
293	All types and functions are in a single \`extern "C"\` FFI module (\`ffi.rs\`), with per-module re-export files providing ergonomic short names:
294	
295	\`\`\`
296	crates/opencascade-sys/generated/
297	├── ffi.rs             # Single extern "C" block with ALL types (full C++ names)
298	├── wrappers.cpp       # Single C++ wrapper file (all includes + wrapper functions)
299	├── gp.rs              # Re-exports: \`pub use crate::ffi::gp_Pnt as Pnt;\` + impl blocks
300	├── topo_ds.rs         # Re-exports for topo_ds module + impl blocks
301	├── ... (per-module files)
302	└── lib.rs             # \`pub(crate) mod ffi;\` + \`pub mod gp;\` etc.
303	\`\`\`
304	
305	Users write \`use opencascade_sys::gp::Pnt;\` — the ffi module is \`pub(crate)\`.
306	
307	### Generator Source
308	
309	\`\`\`
310	crates/opencascade-binding-generator/src/
311	├── main.rs           # CLI entry point
312	├── lib.rs            # Library API (for tests)
313	├── parser.rs         # libclang-based header parser
314	├── model.rs          # IR for parsed declarations (ParsedClass, Method, etc.)
315	├── resolver.rs       # Two-pass symbol table: resolves names, applies filters, builds SymbolTable
316	├── module_graph.rs   # Module dependency analysis
317	├── header_deps.rs    # Automatic header dependency resolution (--resolve-deps)
318	├── type_mapping.rs   # OCCT type -> Rust type mappings
319	└── codegen/
320	    ├── mod.rs
321	    ├── bindings.rs   # ClassBindings IR + emit functions for ffi/cpp/reexports
322	    ├── rust.rs       # Generates ffi.rs + per-module re-export files
323	    ├── cpp.rs        # Generates wrappers.cpp
324	    └── collections.rs # Generates collection type wrappers (iterators, accessors)
325	\`\`\`
326	
327	### Two-Pass Pipeline
328	
329	1. **Parse**: libclang parses OCCT headers into \`ParsedClass\`, \`Method\`, etc. (\`parser.rs\`)
330	2. **Resolve**: \`SymbolTable\` built from parsed data — applies all filters, computes names, determines binding status (\`resolver.rs\`)
331	3. **Generate**: All binding decisions computed into \`ClassBindings\` structs (\`codegen/bindings.rs\`), then Rust and C++ code emitted from them (\`codegen/rust.rs\`, \`codegen/cpp.rs\`)
332	
333	All method filtering (enum checks, lifetime issues, by-value params, etc.) is centralized in \`resolver.rs\` and applied consistently to both FFI and impl generation.
334	
335	### Wrapper Functions
336	
337	All methods use extern "C" C++ wrapper functions, since there is no direct Rust–C++ ABI bridge. The wrappers handle:
338	
339	| C++ Pattern | Wrapper Approach |
340	|-------------|-----------------|
341	| Constructor | \`new T(args)\` returning \`T*\` |
342	| Return by value | \`new T(obj.Method(args))\` returning \`T*\` |
343	| Static method | Free function calling \`ClassName::Method()\` |
344	| \`Handle<T>\` | \`typedef opencascade::handle<T> HandleT;\` |
345	| Overloaded method | Suffix: \`_real3\`, \`_pnt2\`, etc. |
346	| \`const char*\` param | Pass-through as \`const char*\` |
347	| \`const char*\` return | Pass-through as \`const char*\` |
348	| Nullable \`T*\` param | Pass-through as \`T*\` (Rust uses \`Option<&mut T>\`) |
349	| Nullable \`const T*\` param | Pass-through as \`const T*\` (Rust uses \`Option<&T>\`) |
350	| Inherited method | Free function calling \`self->Method()\` |
351	| Upcast (const) | \`Derived_as_Base(self) -> const Base*\` |
352	| Upcast (mut) | \`Derived_as_Base_mut(self) -> Base*\` |
353	| By-value Handle param | Wrapper accepts \`const Handle<T>&\` |
354	| By-value class param | Wrapper accepts \`const T&\` |
355	| Const/mut return fix | \`ConstMutReturnFix\`: const-cast for non-const \`self\` |
356	| \`const char*&\` param (string ref) | Local \`const char*\` var, pass by ref, writeback to Rust-allocated string |
357	| \`&mut\` enum out-param | Local \`int32_t\` var + writeback |
358	| \`&mut\` enum return | \`reinterpret_cast<int32_t*>(&obj.Method())\` returning \`*mut i32\` |
359	| \`const T*\` return | Pass-through as pointer (Rust uses \`Option<&T>\`) |
360	| \`T*\` return (non-const method) | Pass-through as pointer (Rust uses \`Option<&mut T>\`) |
361	| \`T*\` return (const method) | Pass-through as pointer (Rust uses \`Option<&T>\`, downgraded for soundness) |
362	
363	### Handle Support
364	
365	Classes inheriting from \`Standard_Transient\` get:
366	- \`ClassName::to_handle(obj)\` — wrap in \`Handle<T>\`
367	- \`handle.clone()\` — copy the handle (via C++ copy constructor)
368	- \`handle.is_null()\` — check if the handle is null
369	- \`handle.to_handle_base()\` — upcast Handle to base type
370	- \`handle.downcast_to_derived()\` — type-checked downcast
371	- \`handle.get()\` / \`handle.get_mut()\` — dereference handle to contained object
372	
373	
374	
375	### Collection Types
376	
377	NCollection typedefs (e.g., \`TopTools_ListOfShape\`) get iterator wrappers:
378	- C++ iterator struct wrapping \`const_iterator\` or indexed access
379	- \`TypeName_iter()\` / \`TypeNameIterator_next()\` C++ functions
380	- Rust \`Iterator\` trait impl yielding \`OwnedPtr<Element>\`
381	- Impl methods: \`iter()\`, \`from_iter()\`, \`append()\`, etc.
382	
383	### Standard Streams (iostream)
384	
385	OCCT uses \`Standard_OStream\` (typedef for \`std::ostream\`) and \`Standard_IStream\` (typedef for \`std::istream\`) in many debug/dump methods. These are declared as \`manual_types\` in \`bindings.toml\` so the generator recognizes them as known types without generating class bindings. Namespace-scoped typedef aliases (for example \`IMeshData::MapOfInteger\`) are now resolved automatically by guarded parser logic that recognizes OCCT namespace typedef declarations.
386	
387	
388	Manual bindings in the \`standard\` module provide access to the global C++ stream objects:
389	
390	\`\`\`rust
391	use opencascade_sys::standard;
392	use opencascade_sys::b_rep_tools;
393	
394	// Get a mutable reference to std::cout (valid for program lifetime)
395	let cout = standard::cout();
396	
397	// Dump a shape's topological structure to stdout
398	let mut make_box = opencascade_sys::b_rep_prim_api::MakeBox::new_real3(10.0, 20.0, 30.0);
399	let shape = make_box.shape();
400	b_rep_tools::dump_shape_ostream(shape, cout);
401	
402	// Also available: standard::cerr(), standard::clog(), standard::cin()
403	\`\`\`
404	
405	The \`OStream\` and \`IStream\` type aliases are re-exported from the \`standard\` module alongside the auto-generated Standard types.
406	
407	### Naming Conventions
408	
409	- **Types in ffi.rs**: Full C++ names (\`gp_Pnt\`, \`TopoDS_Shape\`, \`BRepPrimAPI_MakeBox\`)
410	- **Types in re-exports**: Short names (\`Pnt\`, \`Shape\`, \`MakeBox\`) via \`pub use crate::ffi::X as Y;\`
411	- **Methods**: snake_case (generated by the code generator)
412	- **Overloads**: Compressed parameter-type suffix (\`_real3\` not \`_real_real_real\`, \`_pnt2\` not \`_pnt_pnt\`)
413	- **Enums**: \`TopAbs_ShapeEnum\` -> \`ShapeEnum\`, variants \`TopAbs_COMPOUND\` -> \`Compound\`
414	- **Reserved names**: \`Vec_\` in ffi, re-exported as \`Vec\`
415	
416	### Manual Bindings
417	
418	Some C++ function signatures can't be auto-generated. Manual replacements live in \`crates/opencascade-sys/manual/\`:
419	- \`<module>.rs\` — \`extern "C"\` declarations + \`impl\` blocks
420	- \`<module>_wrappers.cpp\` — C++ wrapper functions
421	
422	The generator appends \`include!("../manual/<module>.rs");\` (with a comment explaining why) to the generated module re-export file when a corresponding \`manual/<module>.rs\` exists. Because \`include!()\` is a textual insertion, the manual code has full access to the module's type aliases. The \`extern "C"\` declarations in manual files are not marked \`pub\`, so they are private to the module. \`build.rs\` globs \`manual/*_wrappers.cpp\` and compiles them alongside \`generated/wrappers.cpp\`. Since Rust allows multiple \`impl\` blocks for a type, manual methods appear seamlessly alongside the auto-generated ones.
423	
424	Currently only \`standard\` iostream accessors (\`cout()\`, \`cerr()\`, etc.) require manual bindings in \`crates/opencascade-sys/manual/\`. \`bindings.toml\` \`manual_types\` remains useful for explicit opaque known types, while guarded namespace-typedef auto-resolution handles OCCT namespace aliases without per-type config entries.
425	
426	
427	
428	---
429	
430	## Deprecated Symbols
431	
432	The generator does **not** emit bindings for OCCT deprecated symbols. OCCT 8.0.0 moved
433	its backward-compatibility alias headers (e.g. \`TColgp_HArray1OfPnt.hxx\`, now just
434	\`typedef NCollection_HArray1<gp_Pnt>\`) into \`src/Deprecated/\` and pivoted its own API to
435	the canonical \`NCollection_...<T>\` template names. These alias headers are excluded
436	automatically by the \`exclude_deprecated_headers\` config option (on by default), which
437	matches the standard deprecation banner in header content — so bindings target the
438	canonical types rather than the deprecated aliases.
439	
440	## Skipped Symbols
441	
442	The binding generator currently skips **94** symbols (methods, constructors, static methods, and free functions) that it cannot safely represent in Rust FFI. Abstract class constructors are silently omitted since that's expected behavior, not a binding limitation. Every other skipped symbol is documented in generated per-module \`.rs\` files as a \`// SKIPPED:\` comment block including:
443	
444	- **Source location** (header file, line number, C++ symbol name)
445	- **Documentation comment** from the C++ header (first 3 lines)
446	- **Skip reason** explaining why the symbol was excluded
447	- **Commented-out Rust stub** showing the best-guess declaration
448	
449	Example from \`select_mgr.rs\`:
450	\`\`\`rust
451	// SKIPPED: **Source:** \`SelectMgr_BVHThreadPool.hxx\`:101 - \`SelectMgr_BVHThreadPool::Threads\`
452	//   method: Returns array of threads
453	//   Reason: has unbindable types: return: unresolved template type (NCollection_Array1<BVHThread>&)
454	//   // pub fn threads(&mut self) -> /* NCollection_Array1<BVHThread>& */;
455	\`\`\`
456	
457	### Skip Reason Breakdown
458	
459	| Count | % | Category | Description |
460	|------:|----:|----------|-------------|
461	| 66 | 70.2% | **Unknown/unresolved type** | Parameter or return type is not in the resolved known-type set |
462	| 12 | 12.8% | **Rvalue reference** | C++ move semantics (\`T&&\`) — const-ref overloads usually exist |
463	| 10 | 10.6% | **Unknown Handle type** | \`Handle(T)\` where \`T\` is unresolved or excluded |
464	| 2 | 2.1% | **Excluded by bindings.toml** | Explicitly excluded in config |
465	| 2 | 2.1% | **Unresolved template type** | Template instantiations that still cannot be represented safely |
466	| 1 | 1.1% | **Ambiguous overload** | C++ overload would produce conflicting wrapper signatures |
467	| 1 | 1.1% | **Not CppDeletable** | Return type has no destructor in the binding set |
468	
469	Combined unresolved coverage (\`Unknown/unresolved type\` + \`Unknown Handle type\`) is **76 / 94 (80.9%)**.
470	
471	Fixed-size arrays (\`T (&)[N]\`, \`const T (&)[N]\`, and \`T arr[N]\` parameter syntax) are now bindable; there are currently **no** remaining skips categorized as C-style arrays.
472	
473	### Most Common Unknown Types
474	
475	| Count | Type | How to Unblock |
476	|------:|------|----------------|
477	| 5 | \`AVStream const&\` | FFmpeg media type — external dependency |
478	| 5 | \`WNT_HIDSpaceMouse const&\` | Windows-only type, WNT module excluded |
479	| 5 | \`RWGltf_GltfOStreamWriter*\` | RapidJSON-backed writer type — external dependency |
480	| 4 | \`GLXFBConfig\` | X11/Linux display type — platform-specific |
481	| 3 | \`IMeshData_Edge *const const&\` | Internal mesh pointer signature in specialized APIs |
482	| 3 | \`Aspect_XDisplay*\` | X11/Linux display type — platform-specific |
483	| 3 | \`IMeshData_Face *const const&\` | Internal mesh pointer signature in specialized APIs |
484	| 2 | \`NSOpenGLContext*\` | macOS OpenGL context type in platform-specific APIs |
485	| 2 | \`ProxPnt_Status const&\` | Internal proximity/status type not currently in known class set |
486	| 2 | \`AVCodecContext*\` | FFmpeg codec context — external dependency |
487	
488	### Important Skipped Symbols
489	
490	Most skipped symbols are in specialized or platform-specific areas. Current hotspots:
491	
492	**Shape Persistent (7 symbols)** — \`shape_persistent\` dropped significantly after alias normalization; remaining skips are unknown handle instantiations of deeply nested persistence templates (\`pTObject<...>\`, \`ShapePersistent_Poly::instance<...>\`).
493	
494	**UI/Platform Integration (21 symbols)** — \`aspect\` (13), \`graphic3d\` (3), \`osd\` (3), \`v3d\` (1), \`ais\` (1), mostly platform/window-system types (\`GLXFBConfig\`, \`Aspect_XDisplay*\`, \`NSOpenGLContext*\`, and related handles).
495	
496	**Data Exchange (8 symbols)** — \`rw_gltf\` (5), \`iges_control\` (1), \`step_control\` (1), \`rw_stl\` (1). Predominantly external/third-party types, plus \`T&&\` overloads where safe const-ref equivalents are already bound.
497	
498	**Shape Meshing (7 symbols)** — \`i_mesh_data\` (5), \`b_rep_mesh\` (2). \`BRepMesh_Classifier::RegisterWire\` is now bound; remaining skips are internal pointer/handle-heavy signatures.
499	
500	**Geometry (0 symbols in gp/Geom/Geom2d)** — Fully bound for core geometry modules.
501	
502	**Poly (2 symbols)** — one config exclusion and one unresolved type in low-level helper APIs.
503	
504	### How Skipped Symbols Are Tracked
505	
506	All filtering decisions happen in two places:
507	- \`codegen/bindings.rs\`: \`is_method_bindable()\`, \`is_constructor_bindable()\`, \`is_static_method_bindable()\` return \`Result<(), String>\` with a human-readable reason on \`Err\`
508	- \`compute_class_bindings()\` and \`compute_all_function_bindings()\` collect \`SkippedSymbol\` structs for every rejected symbol
509	
510	The \`emit_reexport_class()\` and \`emit_skipped_functions()\` functions write the skip comments to the generated module files.
511	
512	---
513	
514	## Implementation Details
515	
516	The generated code has two layers: a \`pub(crate)\` FFI module containing the raw extern "C" bindings, and public per-module re-export files that provide the user-facing API.
517	
518	### Internal: \`ffi.rs\` (the FFI declarations)
519	
520	A single \`extern "C"\` block declares all types and functions using full C++ names. This is \`pub(crate)\` — users never interact with it directly.
521	
522	Types use their full C++ identifiers as Rust names to avoid collisions:
523	
524	\`\`\`rust
525	// generated/ffi.rs (pub(crate), not user-facing)
526	extern "C" {
527	    // Opaque C++ types -- full C++ names
528	    pub fn gp_Pnt_ctor_real3(theXp: f64, theYp: f64, theZp: f64) -> *mut gp_Pnt;
529	    pub fn gp_Pnt_destructor(self_: *mut gp_Pnt);
530	    pub fn gp_Pnt_x(self_: *const gp_Pnt) -> f64;
531	    pub fn gp_Pnt_set_x(self_: *mut gp_Pnt, theX: f64);
532	    pub fn gp_Pnt_distance(self_: *const gp_Pnt, theOther: *const gp_Pnt) -> f64;
533	    pub fn gp_Pnt_mirrored_pnt(self_: *const gp_Pnt, theP: *const gp_Pnt) -> *mut gp_Pnt;
534	    // ... thousands more
535	}
536	\`\`\`
537	
538	All methods go through extern "C" C++ wrapper functions. There is no ABI-level distinction between "direct" and "wrapped" methods — everything is wrapped for uniform handling.
539	
540	### Internal: \`wrappers.cpp\` (C++ glue)
541	
542	A single C++ file includes all needed OCCT headers and defines \`extern "C"\` wrapper functions for everything:
543	
544	\`\`\`cpp
545	// generated/wrappers.cpp
546	#include <gp_Pnt.hxx>
547	#include <TopoDS_Shape.hxx>
548	// ... OCCT headers
549	
550	extern "C" gp_Pnt* gp_Pnt_ctor_real3(double x, double y, double z) {
551	    return new gp_Pnt(x, y, z);
552	}
553	extern "C" void gp_Pnt_destroy(gp_Pnt* self) {
554	    delete self;
555	}
556	extern "C" double gp_Pnt_x(const gp_Pnt* self) {
557	    return self->X();
558	}
559	// ...
560	\`\`\`
561	
562	### Internal: Per-Module Re-export Files
563	
564	Each module file (e.g., \`gp.rs\`, \`topo_ds.rs\`) re-exports types from \`ffi\` with short names and provides \`impl\` blocks that wrap the internal FFI functions:
565	
566	\`\`\`rust
567	// generated/gp.rs
568	
569	// Type re-export: full C++ name -> short Rust name
570	/// A 3D Cartesian point.
571	pub use crate::ffi::gp_Pnt as Pnt;
572	
573	impl Pnt {
574	    pub fn new_real3(theXp: f64, theYp: f64, theZp: f64) -> crate::OwnedPtr<Self> {
575	        unsafe { crate::OwnedPtr::from_raw(crate::ffi::gp_Pnt_ctor_real3(theXp, theYp, theZp)) }
576	    }
577	
578	    pub fn mirrored_pnt(&self, theP: &crate::ffi::gp_Pnt) -> crate::OwnedPtr<crate::ffi::gp_Pnt> {
579	        unsafe { crate::OwnedPtr::from_raw(crate::ffi::gp_Pnt_mirrored_pnt(self, theP)) }
580	    }
581	
582	    pub fn to_owned(&self) -> crate::OwnedPtr<Self> {
583	        unsafe { crate::OwnedPtr::from_raw(crate::ffi::gp_Pnt_to_owned(self as *const Self)) }
584	    }
585	}
586	\`\`\`
587	
588	### Internal: \`lib.rs\` (Module Structure)
589	
590	\`\`\`rust
591	// generated/lib.rs
592	pub(crate) mod ffi;   // The FFI declarations -- internal only
593	
594	pub mod gp;           // Re-exports gp_Pnt as Pnt, gp_Vec as Vec, etc.
595	pub mod topo_ds;      // Re-exports TopoDS_Shape as Shape, etc.
596	pub mod b_rep_prim_api;
597	pub mod b_rep_algo_api;
598	// ... modules
599	\`\`\`
600	
601	---
602	
603	## Known Issues
604	
605	### UB crash in \`clang\` crate (v2.0.0) — worked around via \`--release\` build
606	
607	The published \`clang\` crate (v2.0.0) has a bug in \`SourceRange::tokenize()\`: it
608	passes the pointer returned by \`clang_tokenize\` directly to
609	\`slice::from_raw_parts\` without a null check. When \`clang_tokenize\` returns a
610	null pointer (which happens for some macro-expanded expressions and compiler
611	builtins), this is undefined behavior. Starting with Rust 1.78, debug builds
612	include UB precondition checks that detect this and abort the process:
613	
614	\`\`\`
615	unsafe precondition(s) violated: slice::from_raw_parts requires the pointer to
616	be aligned and non-null
617	\`\`\`
618	
619	The fix was merged in [PR #58](https://github.com/KyleMayes/clang-rs/pull/58)
620	([issue #47](https://github.com/KyleMayes/clang-rs/issues/47)) but has not been
621	released to crates.io, and later commits in the git repository no longer compile
622	with current Rust. As a workaround, \`scripts/regenerate-bindings.sh\` builds the
623	generator in \`--release\` mode, which disables the debug UB checks. If/when a
624	v2.0.1 is released on crates.io, remove the \`--release\` flag from that script
625	and update \`Cargo.toml\` to use \`version = "2.0"\`.
```
</details>

````markdown
### Collection Iterators

OCCT collection types (NCollection_List, NCollection_Sequence, NCollection_IndexedMap, etc.) get Rust iterator support. Each collection has a C++ iterator wrapper struct and Rust `Iterator` trait impl.

```rust
use opencascade_sys::top_tools::ListOfShape;
use opencascade_sys::topo_ds::Shape;

// Iterate over a list of shapes
for shape in list_of_shape.iter() {
    // shape: OwnedPtr<Shape>
    let x = shape.IsNull();
}

// Build a list from an iterator
let list = ListOfShape::from_iter(shapes.iter());
```
````

**After:**
````markdown
### Collections

Every `NCollection_*<T>` instantiation referenced by the API is materialized under a
canonical name in the `n_collection` module (`List_TopoDS_Shape`, `Array1_gp_Pnt`,
`HArray1_gp_Pnt`, `DataMap_TopoDS_Shape_int`, `IndexedMap_TopoDS_Shape_TopTools_ShapeMapHasher`,
…) with full methods (`new`, `append`/`value`/`set_value`/`add`/`bind`/`find`, …), an
iterator wrapper + `Iterator` impl, and — for handle kinds (`HArray1`/`HSequence`) —
`to_handle`. Collections of primitive scalars (`List_int`, `Sequence_double`) are supported
too; their scalar accessors take/return the value directly.

```rust
use opencascade_sys::n_collection::List_TopoDS_Shape;
use opencascade_sys::topo_ds::Shape;

// Iterate over a list of shapes
let mut it = list_of_shape.iter();
while let Some(shape) = it.next() {
    // shape: OwnedPtr<Shape>
    let x = shape.is_null();
}

let mut list = List_TopoDS_Shape::new();
list.append(a_shape);
```
````

## 🤖🔧 Assistant
<details>
<summary>Edit crates/opencascade-binding-generator/README.md</summary>

**Before:**
````markdown
### FFI Architecture

All types and functions are in a single `extern "C"` FFI module (`ffi.rs`), with per-module re-export files providing ergonomic short names:

```
crates/opencascade-sys/generated/
├── ffi.rs             # Single extern "C" block with ALL types (full C++ names)
├── wrappers.cpp       # Single C++ wrapper file (all includes + wrapper functions)
├── gp.rs              # Re-exports: `pub use crate::ffi::gp_Pnt as Pnt;` + impl blocks
├── topo_ds.rs         # Re-exports for topo_ds module + impl blocks
├── ... (per-module files)
└── lib.rs             # `pub(crate) mod ffi;` + `pub mod gp;` etc.
```

Users write `use opencascade_sys::gp::Pnt;` — the ffi module is `pub(crate)`.
````

**After:**
````markdown
### FFI Architecture

Type definitions live in one file; the `extern "C"` function declarations and their C++
wrapper glue are split per OCCT toolkit (TKernel, TKMath, TKBRep, …) so the C++ and Rust
FFI compile in parallel. Per-module re-export files layer ergonomic short names on top:

```
crates/opencascade-sys/generated/
├── ffi_types.rs         # All opaque/POD type definitions (full C++ names) — pub(crate)
├── ffi_extern_TKMath.rs # extern "C" fn declarations for the TKMath toolkit — pub(crate)
├── ffi_extern_TKBRep.rs # ... one ffi_extern_TK<toolkit>.rs per toolkit (~47 files)
├── wrappers_TKMath.cpp  # C++ wrapper definitions for the TKMath toolkit
├── wrappers_TKBRep.cpp  # ... one wrappers_TK<toolkit>.cpp per toolkit (~47 files)
├── gp.rs                # Re-exports: `pub use crate::ffi_types::gp_Pnt as Pnt;` + impl blocks
├── topo_ds.rs           # Re-exports for topo_ds module + impl blocks
├── ... (per-module files)
└── lib.rs               # `pub(crate) mod ffi_types;` + per-toolkit `mod ffi_extern_TK*;` + `pub mod gp;` etc.
```

Users write `use opencascade_sys::gp::Pnt;` — the `ffi_types` and `ffi_extern_*` modules are
`pub(crate)`. (Internally the generator emits a `crate::ffi::` placeholder for every FFI
reference; the toolkit-split pass rewrites each into `crate::ffi_types::` for a type or
`crate::ffi_extern_TK<toolkit>::` for a function.)
````
</details>

```markdown
- a C++ iterator struct + `TypeNameIterator_next()` function and a Rust `next()`-based
  iterator (`iter()`)
- for handle kinds (`HArray1`/`HSequence`): `to_handle` plus `get`/`get_mut` and the
  handle lifetime machinery on the generated `Handle_*` type

`&NCollection_List<TopoDS_Shape>` and the collection's own methods refer to one type.
```

````markdown
The generated code has two layers: a `pub(crate)` FFI module containing the raw extern "C" bindings, and public per-module re-export files that provide the user-facing API.

### Internal: `ffi.rs` (the FFI declarations)

A single `extern "C"` block declares all types and functions using full C++ names. This is `pub(crate)` — users never interact with it directly.

Types use their full C++ identifiers as Rust names to avoid collisions:

```rust
// generated/ffi.rs (pub(crate), not user-facing)
extern "C" {
    // Opaque C++ types -- full C++ names
    pub fn gp_Pnt_ctor_real3(theXp: f64, theYp: f64, theZp: f64) -> *mut gp_Pnt;
    pub fn gp_Pnt_destructor(self_: *mut gp_Pnt);
    pub fn gp_Pnt_x(self_: *const gp_Pnt) -> f64;
    pub fn gp_Pnt_set_x(self_: *mut gp_Pnt, theX: f64);
    pub fn gp_Pnt_distance(self_: *const gp_Pnt, theOther: *const gp_Pnt) -> f64;
    pub fn gp_Pnt_mirrored_pnt(self_: *const gp_Pnt, theP: *const gp_Pnt) -> *mut gp_Pnt;
    // ... thousands more
}
```

All methods go through extern "C" C++ wrapper functions. There is no ABI-level distinction between "direct" and "wrapped" methods — everything is wrapped for uniform handling.

### Internal: `wrappers.cpp` (C++ glue)

A single C++ file includes all needed OCCT headers and defines `extern "C"` wrapper functions for everything:

```cpp
// generated/wrappers.cpp
#include <gp_Pnt.hxx>
#include <TopoDS_Shape.hxx>
// ... OCCT headers
````

````markdown
The generated code has two layers: a `pub(crate)` FFI layer (type definitions plus
per-toolkit `extern "C"` blocks) containing the raw bindings, and public per-module
re-export files that provide the user-facing API.

### Internal: `ffi_types.rs` + `ffi_extern_TK*.rs` (the FFI declarations)

`ffi_types.rs` declares all types (full C++ names, to avoid collisions), and each
`ffi_extern_TK<toolkit>.rs` declares the `extern "C"` functions for one OCCT toolkit. Both
are `pub(crate)` — users never interact with them directly.

```rust

}
```

All methods go through extern "C" C++ wrapper functions. There is no ABI-level distinction between "direct" and "wrapped" methods — everything is wrapped for uniform handling.

### Internal: `wrappers_TK*.cpp` (C++ glue)

Each `wrappers_TK<toolkit>.cpp` includes the OCCT headers for its toolkit and defines the
`extern "C"` wrapper functions:

```cpp
// generated/wrappers_TKMath.cpp

#include <TopoDS_Shape.hxx>
// ... OCCT headers
````

## Explaining the handle skips (the big one)

This is the single largest gap: **~890 of the ~1,680 skips (53%)** are methods that take or return `Handle(NCollection_HArray1<T>)`, `Handle(NCollection_HSequence<T>)`, or `Handle(NCollection_HArray2<T>)` for some element `T` that isn't registered as handle-able. Concrete example, `GeomAPI_Interpolate::Load`:

**Why:** handle-ability is registered at *parse time* via `bindings.toml`'s `template_instantiations` (the explicit entries) plus the seed list — only those specific instantiations (`HArray1<gp_Pnt>`, `<double>`, `HSequence<TopoDS_Shape>`) are marked handle-able. Every *other* `NCollection_H*<T>` that appears in a signature is picked up by the **auto-inference** pass in [main.rs](crates/opencascade-binding-generator/src/main.rs:339), which hardcodes `handle: false`. So `NCollection_HArray1<bool>` is a *known* type but not a *handle-able* one — the `Handle(...)` wrapper around it resolves to "unknown Handle type" and the method is dropped.

The kicker: `NCollection_HArray1/HArray2/HSequence` all **publicly inherit `Standard_Transient`** (I verified), so they're *legitimately* handle-able. The auto-inference simply doesn't detect it.

## Improvements I'd recommend (in priority order)

1. **Auto-register handle-able `NCollection_H*<T>` instantiations** — the highest-leverage change by far. In the auto-inference pass, when a template's base is a handle-collection (`NCollection_HArray1/HArray2/HSequence`, i.e. inherits `Standard_Transient`), set `handle: true` instead of `false`. That alone would recover most of those ~890 skips. **Caveat** (I hit the analogous issue porting the collections): it must be gated on the element type's header being resolvable — same gate `discover_collections` already uses — otherwise instantiations with un-includable element types would break the C++. The base-type/destructor coordination I built for HArray1/HSequence already handles the collection-vs-template ownership split, so it should slot in.

Here's the full derivation of that name.

## The pieces

**`top_exp`** — `TopExp` is an OCCT *utility class* (only static methods, no instances). The generator turns those into module-level free functions, so `TopExp` → module `top_exp` and the method `MapShapes` → `map_shapes`.

**Why a suffix at all** — `TopExp::MapShapes` is overloaded **three** times, and all three would become the free function `map_shapes` → a name collision. So the generator appends a parameter-type suffix computed by `overload_suffix_from_params` ([model.rs:1123](crates/opencascade-binding-generator/src/model.rs:1123)):

```rust

type_names = params.map(|p| p.ty.short_name().to_lowercase())
// ["real","real","real"] -> "real3";  ["bool","bool"] -> "bool2"
```

The three overloads and their suffixes:

| C++ overload | Suffix |
|---|---|
| `MapShapes(const TopoDS_Shape&, const TopAbs_ShapeEnum, NCollection_IndexedMap<TopoDS_Shape, TopTools_ShapeMapHasher>&)` | `_shape_shapeenum_indexedmap_topods_shape_toptools_shapemaphasher` |
| `MapShapes(const TopoDS_Shape&, NCollection_IndexedMap<…>&, bool=true, bool=true)` | `_shape_indexedmap_topods_shape_toptools_shapemaphasher_bool2` |
| `MapShapes(const TopoDS_Shape&, NCollection_Map<…>&, bool=true, bool=true)` | `_shape_map_topods_shape_toptools_shapemaphasher_bool2` |

## Where each fragment comes from (overload #1)

- `const TopoDS_Shape& S` → `short_name("TopoDS_Shape")` = `Shape` → **`shape`**
- `const TopAbs_ShapeEnum T` → `short_name("TopAbs_ShapeEnum")` = `ShapeEnum` → **`shapeenum`**
- `NCollection_IndexedMap<TopoDS_Shape, TopTools_ShapeMapHasher>& M` → **`indexedmap_topods_shape_toptools_shapemaphasher`**

The `bool2` in the other two is just the two trailing default-`bool` params (`cumOri`, `cumLoc`) compressed as a repeat count.

## Why the map fragment is so long

`short_name()` ([model.rs:982](crates/opencascade-binding-generator/src/model.rs:982)) only strips the leading module prefix (the part up to the first `_`) and returns the rest. For a plain class that's clean — `TopoDS_Shape` → `Shape`. But the map parameter is a **template instantiation**, and by the time the suffix is computed its Rust type name is the *mangled canonical* form `NCollection_IndexedMap_TopoDS_Shape_TopTools_ShapeMapHasher` (produced by `config::template_alias_name`, which flattens `<`, `>`, and `,` into `_`). `short_name()` drops only the leading `NCollection_` and lowercases the rest — so the **entire template argument list survives in the suffix**: the element `TopoDS_Shape` *and* the hasher `TopTools_ShapeMapHasher`.

So the length is really the hasher's fault. This is also a case where the 8.0 canonical-names pivot made it uglier: pre-8.0 that parameter's type was the alias `TopTools_IndexedMapOfShape`, which would have abbreviated to `indexedmapofshape` (no explicit hasher). Now the canonical `NCollection_IndexedMap<TopoDS_Shape, TopTools_ShapeMapHasher>` spells the hasher out, and the suffix inherits all of it.

That's why improvement #3 from my last message would help: give collection template instantiations a shorter suffix token (e.g. drop the hasher argument, or use a curated short alias) so overloads like this read `map_shapes_shape_shapeenum_indexedmapofshape` instead of the current mouthful — the suffix generator is the single place (`Type::short_name` for collection types) where that would be fixed.

```
/// Build the short overload-suffix token for a collection, e.g. `imap_shape`,
```

```
    /// Token used to build overload suffixes. Same as [`short_name`](Self::short_name)
    /// except collection types use a concise registered token (`imap_shape`, `arr1_pnt`,
    /// `harr1_pnt`) instead of the verbose mangled name (which carries the full template
    /// argument list including the hasher).
    pub fn suffix_token(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Type::ConstRef(inner) | Type::MutRef(inner) | Type::RValueRef(inner) => {
                inner.suffix_token()
            }
            Type::ConstPtr(inner) | Type::MutPtr(inner) => format!("{}ptr", inner.suffix_token()),
            Type::FixedArray(inner, size) => format!("{}{}", inner.suffix_token(), size),
            Type::Class(name) => crate::codegen::collections::collection_suffix_token(name)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| extract_short_name(name)),
            Type::Handle(name) => crate::codegen::collections::collection_suffix_token(name)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| crate::type_mapping::handle_param_name(name)),
            _ => self.short_name(),
        }
    }
```

```
/// An owned iterator (e.g. a collection's `iter()` result, an owned `IterX`) is itself an
/// `Iterator`, so it works directly in `for` loops and iterator adapters:
/// `for item in collection.iter() { ... }`.
impl<T: CppDeletable + Iterator> Iterator for OwnedPtr<T> {
    type Item = T::Item;

    #[inline]
    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
        (**self).next()
    }
}
```

```markdown
| ~14 | **Rvalue reference** | C++ move semantics (`T&&`) — const-ref overloads usually exist. |

The single biggest lever for coverage is auto-registering handle-able
`NCollection_H*<T>` instantiations (rather than the current curated
`template_instantiations` list) — that alone would recover over half the skips.

Fixed-size arrays (`T (&)[N]`, `const T (&)[N]`, and `T arr[N]` parameter syntax) are bindable; there are **no** remaining skips categorized as C-style arrays. Core geometry (`gp`/`Geom`/`Geom2d`) and topology/modeling modules are essentially fully bound; remaining skips concentrate in the handle-collection APIs above and in platform/window-system and external-dependency types (X11 `GLXFBConfig`/`Aspect_XDisplay*`, macOS `NSOpenGLContext*`, FFmpeg/glTF writer types, etc.).
```

```
Upgrade to OCCT 8.0.0; pivot collections to canonical NCollection names; expand coverage

match OCCT 8.0's API, which now uses the canonical `NCollection_*<T>` templates
directly and deprecated the old `TColgp_*`/`TColStd_*`/`TopTools_*` aliases.

Binding generator:
- Exclude deprecated 8.0 backward-compat alias headers automatically
  (`exclude_deprecated_headers`), so bindings target canonical NCollection types.
- Auto-discover NCollection instantiations from referenced template spellings and
  generate them under canonical `n_collection::` names with full method sets,
  including collections of primitive scalars and `HArray1`/`HSequence` handle
  collections (`to_handle`, `get`/`get_mut`).

High-level crate, examples, and tests:
- Port `opencascade` and all in-repo examples to the canonical names and new idioms.
- Regenerate the golden STEP files for OCCT 8.0 (version-string change only).

Docs: rewrite README/PORTING to describe the split FFI layout, canonical
collections, handle naming, and a C++-to-Rust plus pre-8.0 migration guide.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

All three improvements are implemented, verified, documented, and committed.

## Summary

**#1 — Auto-register handle-able `NCollection_H*<T>` instantiations.** In `collect_template_class_types` I now also collect template spellings inside `Type::Handle(...)` (the missing piece — most handle-collections appear as `Handle(NCollection_HArray1<T>)`, not as a bare class), and the auto-inference sets `handle: true` for the `HArray1`/`HArray2`/`HSequence` bases (they inherit `Standard_Transient`). Also made the collection the sole owner of its handle machinery so the per-toolkit loop doesn't double-define it. **Skipped symbols dropped 1,679 → 721; handle-collection skips 892 → 8.**

**#2 — `Iterator` trait for collection iterators.** Each iterator now `impl Iterator` (was an inherent `next()`), plus a blanket `impl<T: CppDeletable + Iterator> Iterator for OwnedPtr<T>` in `owned_ptr.rs`, so `for x in coll.iter()` and adapters work. Modernized the high-level crate's manual `while let` loops to for-loops.

**#3 — Shortened collection overload-suffix tokens.** A thread-local registry maps each collection's mangled name to a concise token (`imap_shape`, `arr1_pnt`, `harr1_pnt`, `dmap_shape_int` — dropping the hasher), consumed by a new `Type::suffix_token()`. Collisions are absorbed by the existing `_N` de-collision. `map_shapes_shape_shapeenum_indexedmap_topods_shape_toptools_shapemaphasher` → `map_shapes_shape_shapeenum_imap_shape`; `Interpolate::new_handlencollectionharray1gppnt_bool_real` → `new_harr1_pnt_bool_real`.

**Consumers & docs.** Ported the 6 renamed methods in the `opencascade` crate + examples (including `load` → `load_vec2_bool`, since #1 un-skipped its second overload), adopted the for-loop idiom, and updated both READMEs + PORTING.md (skip counts, breakdown, handle auto-registration, `Iterator`/for-loop, short suffix tokens). Updated top-level README counts (~720 skips, ~8,000 types, ~144,000 fns).

**Verification:** 22 generator tests, full `cargo build`, and 33 workspace tests all green (goldens unchanged — geometry identical).

**Commit:** `374d024` "Upgrade to OCCT 8.0.0; pivot collections to canonical NCollection names; expand coverage" — 496 files, capturing this whole session's OCCT 8.0 arc (submodule bump, generator changes, high-level port, golden regen, docs). Session logs were intentionally left uncommitted.
